verifiedAgainstRegulations.detail: The service publishes geography the authority's own current regulations say no longer exists. The 2026 summary states: "Deer management units 351 and 352 have been rescinded" and "The limited firearms deer zone has been eliminated." Both DMU-351 (Mideast Upper Peninsula) and DMU-352 (Midwest Upper Peninsula unit) are still returned by the layer, stamped Year='2026' like every other row and last edited 2026-09-22, and the LimitedFirearmZoneBoundary layer is still published. Verified live 2026-09-23. Michigan's map may therefore NOT be served as the service returns it: drawing 351 or 352 would show a hunter a rescinded unit as current, and no field on the layer distinguishes them — Year does not, because it says 2026 for all 115 rows.
verifiedAgainstRegulations.consequence: Parity against the authority's own GIS service is NOT sufficient certification here, because the service is the thing that is out of date. Michigan's map lane must be certified against the REGULATIONS as well as against the service, and the rescinded units excluded by an explicit, sourced exclusion list rather than by a rule inferred from the data.

geography.alsoUnreferenced: The 2026 summary does not mention DMU-333 (Lansing core CWD area), DMU-419 (Lansing CWD management zone), DMU-486 or DMU-487 (multicounty units) or DMU-499 (Urban deer management zone) at all, though it does sell a "DMU 487 antlerless deer license". Read on the dataset's own ArcGIS item; michigan.gov refuses automated clients, so the terms were read in the browser pane rather than by script. XII written descriptions are the law and the mapped units are "condensed summaries", and the still-published LimitedFirearmZoneBoundary layer was eliminated by regulation for 2026 and must not be drawn. A point at the Lansing capitol returns THREE overlapping DMUs (033 Ingham County, 486 Southern Lower Peninsula, 333 Lansing CWD core) — a legitimate nesting of county, multicounty and disease geography, not a data conflict, and a state that will exercise overlapping-zone resolution properly.

servingDecision.reason: Michigan is NOT served, and the licence is not what blocks it — the licence is clear. The rescission of DMU 351 and DMU 352 is established as a FACT but not as an INSTRUMENT. Minutes of the adopting vote are evidence that a thing was decided; they are not the instrument that decided it. Nobody has read the repealing sentence, and there is no effective date. There is no version of serving this that is honest.

exclusionList.conformedTextNote: The conformed text as adopted is NOT PUBLISHED so far as we can establish: nine filename variants were probed across five 2026 NRC folders and all returned 404. Recorded as UNREAD, not as non-existent — 'we could not read it' is never 'it does not exist'. The candidate Signed_06WCO2026_Action_Edited.pdf is the right amendment number and the wrong version: it predates the meeting (ModDate 2026-04-15) and still contains sections 3.124, 12.483, 12.484, 1.2(17) and 2.1(4) unstruck.

servingDecision.neverCertifyFrom: THE CONSOLIDATED WILDLIFE CONSERVATION ORDER. WCO.pdf and every chapter PDF carry amendment history only through Am. 5 of 2026 (eff. 2026-04-08) and still contain the rescinded sections 3.124, 12.483 and 12.484 and the eliminated limited-firearms-zone definitions 1.2(17) and 2.1(4). It is the obvious document for a future agent to reach for, and certifying Michigan deer from it would reproduce exactly the defect this decision refuses to ship.

precedence.evidence: Not merely unfound — absent by drafting choice, which is a stronger finding. Across 183 pages: 'precedence' 0 hits, 'supersede' 0, 'most restrictive' 0, 'shall govern' 0, 'shall control' 0, 'overlap' 0. The single 'more restrictive … shall prevail' concerns federal versus state migratory-bird permits, not geography. Where the drafters wanted mutual exclusion they wrote it into the definitions — §12.19b defines its unit as counties 'except those lands defined in section 12.33a' — so the absence elsewhere is deliberate. Units 486, 487, 499 and 333 genuinely overlap the county units and nothing resolves them: evaluate every containing unit and return CONFLICT.

servingDecision.kindNotDerivable: A unit's kind must be assigned per Chapter XII section and stored as data, never inferred. Decisive on its own: the layer contains code 261, which does not occur anywhere in the Wildlife Conservation Order. The GIS also contradicts the Order twice — DMU-499's GIS heading says 'Urban deer management zone' while §12.499's operative sentence defines a 'January archery deer management zone', and 359's number never appears in the body of its own section. Number ranges do not encode kind either (349/351, 354/359 and 486/487/499 are different kinds within the same hundreds).
servingDecision.unitsThatGovernNothing: DMU-486 governs nothing in the Order: the string 486 occurs only inside §12.486 itself. It is a licence-administration and mapping construct. DMU-487 by contrast is a row in §3.105a Table 4, which is why an antlerless licence for it is sellable.
servingDecision.lowerPeninsulaIsCounty: CONFIRMED from the Order's own words: 'establish limits on the number of universal antlerless deer licenses that hunters could use for each deer management unit in the Upper Peninsula and each county in the Lower Peninsula.' The Order's table is literally keyed two ways — the UP column headed 'Deer Management Unit', the LP column headed 'County'. Fifteen Lower Peninsula DMUs (161, 162, 261, 262, 311, 312, 332, 341, 354, 359, 361, 452, 486, 487, 499) are not coterminous with counties, so a county-keyed limit CANNOT be resolved by DMU lookup. Michigan's Lower Peninsula cannot be answered until county geography exists, with its own licence reviewed to the same standard as any unit layer.
servingDecision.askedOfAuthority: The conformed text of WCO Amendment No. 6 of 2026 as adopted, and its effective date.

theAuthoritysOwnMapContradictsItsOwnMinu.finding: MDNR's own published DMU layer STILL CARRIES DMU 351 and DMU 352. Queried directly: 115 features, and both codes are present.
theAuthoritysOwnMapContradictsItsOwnMinu.andTheyAreNotLEFTOVERS: Both are tagged Year 2026, created 2026-09-21 and last edited 2026-09-21 — FOUR MONTHS AFTER the Natural Resources Commission's 2026-05-13 vote to rescind them. The whole layer carries exactly one distinct Year value, 2026. So this is not a stale prior-season edition that nobody refreshed; it is the authority republishing the current season's units, after the vote, with both units in it.
theAuthoritysOwnMapContradictsItsOwnMinu.whatThisDoesNOTEstablish: That the units exist in law. A government GIS attribute is not the instrument — the same rule that stops minutes being the instrument stops the map being one. At least three readings fit the evidence and nothing here chooses between them: the rescission may not have taken effect for the 2026 season (no effective date was ever found); the GIS may lag the order; or the amendment may not have been conformed as adopted.
theAuthoritysOwnMapContradictsItsOwnMinu.whatItDoesEstablish: That the contradiction is REAL, DATED and on the authority's own systems, rather than a gap in our reading. Before this, the record said the rescission was a fact without an instrument. It is now a fact without an instrument that the authority's own current map disagrees with.
theAuthoritysOwnMapContradictsItsOwnMinu.whyItStrengthensUNAVAILABLE: Serving Michigan on the minutes would have dropped two units the authority is still publishing; serving on the GIS would have kept two units its Commission voted to rescind. Both directions are wrong on this evidence, which is what UNAVAILABLE is for.
theAuthoritysOwnMapContradictsItsOwnMinu.theQuestionToPUT: This converts an open research task into one concrete question for MDNR: what is the effective date of Wildlife Conservation Order Amendment No. 6 of 2026 as adopted, and are DMUs 351 and 352 in force for the 2026 season? The GIS edition date makes that answerable rather than speculative.

controllingInstrumentFound.conclusion: THE RESCISSION TOOK LEGAL EFFECT ON 2026-05-24. Both DEFINING sections (12.483, 12.484) and the REGULATION section that governed hunting in them (3.124) are repealed by Amendment No. 6 of 2026 — the same amendment the Commission's 2026-05-13 minutes recorded. Deer management units 351 and 352 do not exist in Michigan law.

whatThisSettles.theEffectiveDateWasUNKNOWN: It is 2026-05-24, eleven days after the vote. The record previously warned that 'Sept. 12, 2026' from the regulations summary was the Liberty Hunt opening day and would have been a plausible-wrong effective date; it was right to refuse it.
whatThisSettles.theConformedTextWasUNREAD: Nine filename variants across five 2026 NRC folders had 404'd. The conformed text is not published as a standalone amendment document — it is published CONSOLIDATED INTO the Wildlife Conservation Order, which is where a repeal lives once it takes effect.
whatThisSettles.theMinutesWereRight: and were still not the instrument. Treating them as one would have reached the right answer for the wrong reason, and would have reached a wrong one wherever a vote is later amended, delayed or not conformed.
whatThisSettles.theGISIsSTALE: MDNR's own layer still publishes both units, created and last edited 2026-09-21 — four months AFTER the repeal took effect. A government GIS attribute is not the instrument, which is exactly what this case now demonstrates in the direction that matters: the map is wrong and the order is right.

controllingInstrumentFound.productConsequence: Michigan's deer geography is the authority's own published layer MINUS deer management units 351 and 352, which the adapter expresses as a quarantine with its reason — the mechanism Idaho already uses for Yellowstone National Park. discovery.whyThisStateIsTheMostCompleteSoFar: Utah publishes geometry AND the hunt join in one place: layer 0 holds 686 named hunt boundaries, and table 1 (NRDWRGIS.%HUNT_INFO_MOBILE) holds 3,037 rows keyed BOUNDARY_NAME / BOUNDARYID / HUNT_NUMBER / SEASON. So hunt number → boundary → season is resolvable from the authority alone, which is the shape Hunt needs and is rarer than the geometry.
discovery.speciesSpecificGeography: Utah does NOT discriminate species on the boundary layer. Its BTYPE field is null or empty for almost every row — only "CWMU" is populated — so which species and class a boundary serves comes from the HUNT_NUMBER in the join table (for example DB1348), not from the polygon. Anything grouping Utah's geography by a layer attribute would find nothing.
discovery.seasonsAreNotAllPublished: Some SEASON values are not dates: "Contact CWMU Operator for 2026 season dates". Cooperative Wildlife Management Unit seasons are deferred to a private operator, so those hunts are a genuine UNKNOWN even with the join in hand and must never be rendered as a season.
discovery.writtenDescriptionsExist: Each boundary carries a written metes-and-bounds Description. Maine's precedent here is that where a written description accompanies a polygon the description may control; Utah states no precedence either way, and it has not been established.

discovery.howFound: Layer name search, then confirmed by host (geodata.hawaii.gov) and by the layer's own copyrightText.
discovery.whyThisIsTheStrongestUSFinDING: It is the only US layer found so far that cites the regulation it implements: its description names HAR Title 13 Chapters 122 and 123 and links DOFAW's published PDFs. Geometry, species applicability and the governing rule arrive together.
discovery.speciesApplicabilityIsOnThePolYGON: Fields mammal_uni and bird_unit carry SEPARATE mammal and bird unit designations, and status distinguishes them: Hunting Area (Mammal and Bird) 81, Hunting Area (Mammal ONLY) 35, Hunting Area (Bird ONLY) 5. So one polygon can be open to mammals and closed to birds, and a model that treated "hunting area" as one geography would answer the wrong species.
discovery.theLayerAlsoHoldsCLOSURES: Of 186 polygons only 121 are hunting areas. The rest are CLOSED 13, No Hunting 16, Safety Zone 19 and Safety Zone (NO HUNTING) 17. Counting the layer's feature count as a unit count would overstate Hawaii's huntable geography by 54 percent and, worse, could draw a safety zone as a hunting unit.
discovery.islands: Hawaii, Kauai, Lanai, Maui, Molokai, Oahu — all six, in an island field, which is the geography §39 asks to be treated on its own terms.

geography.term: Wildlife Management Unit (WMU); the Oregon Administrative Rules call the same thing a "wildlife unit"
geography.definedBy: Oregon Administrative Rules chapter 635, Division 080 "WILDLIFE UNITS" — one rule per unit, 635-080-0010 (Saddle Mountain) through 635-080-0077 (Fort Rock). OAR 635-080-0000: for the purpose of managing Oregon's wildlife the State has been divided into separate described areas called wildlife units. The boundary definition is TEXTUAL; the GIS is a depiction of it, and ODFW's own licence note says so by pointing at the OAR division.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The layer returns 69 features. 67 are managed units (REGION EAST 47, WEST 20); TWO are REGION='NOT MANAGED' — UNIT_NUM 0 'WARM SPRING INDIAN RESERVATION' and UNIT_NUM 1 'CRATER LAKE NP'. Counting 69 would overstate Oregon's unit system by two AND would draw a reservation and a national park as huntable management units. Corroborated independently: unit numbers run 10–77 with 13 absent, which is exactly 67, and matches the OAR division's per-unit rule numbering.

licence.statedAs: Boundaries may not be altered without permission of the Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife. For official legal boundary description see: https://secure.sos.state.or.us/oard/displayDivisionRules.action?selectedDivision=2968
licence.attribution: Oregon Department of Fish and Wildlife
licence.note: A restriction on ALTERATION, which is not a restriction on USE. "Boundaries may not be altered without permission" forbids changing the geometry; it says nothing about drawing it, querying it or redistributing it unchanged. So UNRESOLVED rather than RESTRICTED — classifying an alteration clause as a use refusal would be the over-strict error §8 treats as equally false. It DOES bear on §41B's simplification: a zoom-generalised copy is arguably an altered boundary, and that question is unresolved and load-bearing for how Oregon could ever be drawn.

discovery.howFound: Host nrimp.dfw.state.or.us, ODFW's own, corroborated by four separate ODFW staff accounts publishing the same 69-unit layer.
discovery.regulationsLead: The licence links the Oregon Administrative Rules division carrying the official legal boundary descriptions — a regulations source arriving inside a licence, which is unusual and worth keeping.

temporalBreak.finding: Eastern Oregon DEER changed management geography in 2026. The official artifact's "What's new for 2026" (p. 13): a shift from Wildlife Management Units to deer hunt areas, with new hunt names and numbers. ODFW's own article (https://myodfw.com/articles/eastern-oregon-deer-hunts, dated 2025-11-21) explains it: from 2026 eastern Oregon deer hunts are organized by Deer Hunt Areas instead of WMUs, built on 22 mule deer herd ranges identified from over 1,400 GPS-collared deer, renamed alphanumerically (NE-01).
temporalBreak.whyItMatters: A 2025 answer keyed to WMUs is WRONG for 2026 eastern Oregon deer, and a 2026 answer is wrong for 2025. This is a change of geographic IDENTITY, not a boundary adjustment, so no amount of reprojection reconciles them.
temporalBreak.howTheYearIsCarried: By SERVICE NAME, not by a field — the more dangerous form, because a schema check for is_active, year_deactivated or an effective date finds nothing and looks clean. No temporal field exists on any layer. 100Series_HuntBoundary_2026, 400Series_, 500Series_, 700Series_, MD_HuntAreas ("2026"), MD_HerdRanges ("2026"). Searching the owning account for 2025 equivalents returned only the 2026 set, so prior years are retired rather than kept: a stored snapshot cannot answer a past year, and a hard-coded 2026 URL will silently answer the WRONG year once ODFW publishes 2027.

speciesGeography.pattern: SEPARATE ANNUAL LAYERS, one per controlled-hunt series — not an attribute on one layer.
speciesGeography.theOneCharacterTrap: Two services differ by a single character. 100Series_HuntBoundary_2026 (singular) holds BUCK deer at layer 7, 162 features. 100Series_HuntBoundaries_2026 (plural) holds ANTLERLESS deer at layer 1, 72 features. Worse, the portal item pointing at the plural service is TITLED "600Series_HuntBoundaries_2026". Picking by service name alone silently swaps buck and antlerless geography — the same class of hazard as Nevada's.
speciesGeography.layerIdsAreNotZero: Layer ids are 7, 1, 19, 21, 3. A layer-0 assumption fails on almost all of them.
speciesGeography.classIsInTheData: The buck-deer layer's Animal field separates 'One buck with visible antler' (115), 'One mule deer buck with visible antler' (14), 'One white-tailed deer buck with visible antler' (8), 'One white-tailed deer' (8), 'One deer' (6) — so mule, white-tailed and black-tailed deer and the antlered/antlerless class are all distinguished inside one nominal species, which is §16's sex/age-versus-regulatory-class separation arriving as real data.
speciesGeography.theWMUIsOnlyTheBase: Most big-game seasons are set by controlled-hunt areas DERIVED from WMUs: "Hunt Area Entire Wildlife Management Unit unless indicated with an asterisk(*)", with textual controlled-hunt descriptions appended (pp. 94–103). The hunt-boundary layers carry UnitType = full unit (140), subunit (17), multiunit (5) and a HuntDesc field holding the authority's prose. So a coordinate resolves to a WMU, and the applicable hunt area is a full, partial or multi-WMU composite of it, per species and per year.
speciesGeography.gameBirds: No ODFW-owned GIS for waterfowl zones or upland regions was located from any _ODFW or ODFW_AGO account.

theFindThatOutweighsTheLicence.layer0: UnitSpatial — 367 polygons, ONE layer covering every WDFW regulated hunting geography, not just GMUs.
theFindThatOutweighsTheLicence.layer1: A STRUCTURED REGULATION TABLE, 30,621 records, on WDFW's own host. This is the highest-value single artifact found anywhere in the United States sweep: the regulations as data rather than as a PDF to be extracted. §44 asks for machine-readable authoritative data before scraping, and Washington published it.
theFindThatOutweighsTheLicence.whyItIsRecordedHereAndNotActedOn: A reachable, structured, authoritative artifact is not a licence to store it. The terms remain unresolved, so this is recorded as the reason to resolve them — it is the strongest case in the country for asking, and that ask is the owner's under the no-contact constraint.

CONDITIONS, NOT A REFUSAL — and I am recording a classification I do not share. The discovery pass classified this RESTRICTED. Read against its own words it is not: there is no prohibition on use, reproduction or redistribution anywhere in it. What it states is attribution ("should be clearly cited in any product derived from this Data"), a describe-your-changes condition, an indemnity and a warranty disclaimer. Both of the first two PRESUPPOSE that derived products are permissible — you cannot be required to cite and to describe modifications in a product you may not make. That is materially stronger than Oregon, which restricts alteration outright. But conditions are not a grant either, so UNRESOLVED both ways. §8 is explicit that a restriction stricter than the source is as false as a looser one, and RESTRICTED here would be the strict error: it would park a state whose publisher anticipates derived products.

WHERE IT WAS FOUND MATTERS: the portal ITEM's licenseInfo, not the service. Service-level copyrightText on both PGC_Boundaries and PGC_Hunting_Boundaries is an EMPTY STRING — the New Mexico and Nevada pattern, where reading the service alone returns nothing and looks like silence. The same statement was independently read from four further PGC items (PGC Hunting Boundaries, DMAP Units, CWD, State Game Lands), so it is the account's standard text rather than one layer's.

conflict.finding:
TWO OF THE AUTHORITY'S OWN HOSTS DISAGREE, on two separate layers. Pennsylvania publishes from ArcGIS Online org k8yxvICm95iIFicb (account PAGameCommissionGIS) AND from its own on-premise server pgcmaps.pa.gov, and the two do not match:

  Hunting Hours    —  7 meridian bands on ArcGIS Online, 6 on pgcmaps.pa.gov.
Both hosts are the Game Commission's. Neither is obviously stale.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: Picking the larger count, the smaller count, or the newer modified date would each be an invention. §8 provides CONFLICT as a state precisely so that this is reportable without being decided, and the elk layer is the one that matters most: elk licences are allocated by zone, so answering 11 where the law uses 14 would send hunters to the wrong zone with a valid-looking answer.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: 58 Pa. Code § 139.18 defines the elk zones textually. Reading that section decides the elk conflict from the instrument rather than from either GIS copy. The hours bands resolve the same way, against Appendix G's own meridian figure.

discovery.howFound: Owner PAGameCommissionGIS in org k8yxvICm95iIFicb, plus the agency's own on-premise server pgcmaps.pa.gov. That false negative is why no state was ever recorded as "searched and found nothing" on the strength of that tool.

geography.term: COUNTY — Missouri publishes no statewide hunting-unit grid
geography.definedBy: The Wildlife Code of Missouri, Title 3 (Department of Conservation), Division 10 (Conservation Commission), Chapter 7, published by the Missouri Secretary of State. The Code sets deer and turkey regulations BY COUNTY; 115 county polygons are the operative geography, and waterfowl uses its own zones.
geography.theAbsenceIsTheFinding: Missouri does not have a WMU/GMU/unit system, and looking for one is how a state gets recorded as having no geography when it has four. §9 warns against hard-coding one jurisdiction's terminology into a universal model, and Missouri is the case that bites: a resolver that requires a unit layer finds nothing here, while a resolver that accepts the authority's own geography finds counties, deer/turkey county rules and waterfowl zones. Counties are a published Census-and-state geography, so the usual objection — no official polygons — does not apply. What is missing is not geography; it is the zone service, below.

reachability.finding: MDC's own hunting-zone service, gisblue.mdc.mo.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Boundaries/Hunting_Zones/MapServer, does not complete a connection at all — HTTP 0, no response, not a 4xx or 5xx. That service is the one holding Missouri's waterfowl and other published zone geography, so the zones cannot be read even though the county half of the geography can.

evidence.positiveControlSameSweep: services1.arcgis.com/BEFhRGD6ppzvv08z .../Missouri_Counties/FeatureServer/0 returned 200 with 115 features, so the sweep's own fetching worked.

reachability.whyNotWorkedAround: There is no workaround that stays inside §8. A county layer is not a waterfowl zone, and substituting one for the other would answer a zone question with a geography the rule does not use. Nor is a third-party copy acceptable: §44 requires the authority's own service.
reachability.whatWouldUnblockIt: The host responding. It is MDC's own server on MDC's own domain, so this is theirs to fix, and asking is the owner's under the no-contact constraint.
reachability.notTheSameAsLicenceBlocked: Missouri's terms were partly readable and are recorded below. This is a transport failure on one service, not a refusal — the two are undone by completely different actions.

threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.statedAs: You may not reproduce this site's text, images, or videos without the Department’s written permission.
threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.readsOn: SITE CONTENT — text, images, videos. An express prohibition, and the only express prohibition Missouri states. It does not name data, datasets, geometry or GIS services, and reading it onto them would be the merge this field exists to prevent: it would block Missouri on a sentence about photographs.

threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.statedAs: Although all data in this data set have been compiled by the Missouri Department of Agriculture, no warranty, expressed or implied, is made by the department as to the accuracy of the data…
threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.readsOn: A WARRANTY DISCLAIMER, and from a different department (Agriculture, not Conservation). It grants nothing and refuses nothing.
An ATTRIBUTION string, complete and verbatim. Not terms at all.

termsReadElsewhere.conclusion: So Missouri has one express prohibition that is about its website, one foreign-department warranty disclaimer, and one attribution string. No instrument states reuse terms for the hunting geography. Classifying the state RESTRICTED on the strength of the website sentence would be the strict error §8 forbids; classifying it permitted would be the loose one. The transport failure is what actually blocks it today.

legalHours.finding: PER SPECIES, and one species states none. There is no single statewide hours rule. From the Wildlife Code, 3 CSR 10-7: deer 10-7.431(4), elk 10-7.700(3) and black bear 10-7.900(4) are each "from one-half (1/2) hour before sunrise until one-half (1/2) hour after sunset". Spring turkey 10-7.455(1)(A)1 runs to 1:00 p.m. CDT on PUBLIC land and to sunset on PRIVATE land. Migratory birds 10-7.440 — doves, rails, woodcock, snipe, ducks, coots and geese — close AT sunset. Rabbits 10-7.420(1) run BETWEEN sunrise and sunset. Squirrels 10-7.425 state a season and limits and NO HOURS AT ALL.
threeThingsThatBreakASingleModel: The big-game window is asymmetric (half an hour before sunrise, half an hour AFTER sunset) while migratory birds close AT sunset. One offset pair cannot be both, and using the big-game pair for ducks would authorise shooting after legal light.
Spring turkey needs a PUBLIC-versus-PRIVATE LAND discriminator before its window can be stated, and its 1:00 p.m. cutoff is written in CDT — a named civil clock, not a solar term.

Squirrels state no hours. §8: that is an unresolved evidentiary gap, not a default. Filling it with the big-game rule would invent a restriction the Code does not impose, and filling it with sunrise-to-sunset would invent a different one.
legalHours.whyNoStateLevelHoursRecordWasAdded: The hours registry holds ONE record per state with one basis. Missouri does not have one basis, so any entry there would be a rounding of the source into the nearest existing field — exactly what §41A forbids. The registry's per-state shape is the limitation, and naming it here is the honest move; expanding it to per-species is real work and is not done by writing a wrong record now.

Everything before it reads permissively — attribution, describe-your-modifications, don't-misrepresent, a scale allowance, warranty disclaimers — and on the 2023 edition the prohibition is literally the final sentence.

THE TRUNCATION WOULD HAVE INVERTED THE ANSWER. My discovery tool stores 1,200 characters of item licence text and the sweep printed 400. At 400 characters Alaska looks exactly like Pennsylvania: conditions that presuppose derived products, no refusal. I would have recorded UNRESOLVED-leaning-permissive on a state that refuses outright. The rule this confirms is that a licence is classified from its whole text or not at all.

TWO EDITIONS, DIFFERENT TERMS, AND THEY MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. Effective 7/1/2023 the scale allowance is 1:250,000 and the prohibition is phrased "by a 3rd-party ... is strictly prohibited"; effective 7/1/2025 the allowance is 1:63,360 — FINER, so more permissive — while the prohibition widens from "3rd-party" to "Users". Citing the wrong edition misstates both halves, in opposite directions. The recorded text is the current 2025 one, from item f1019b8731aa4ec4921501d035c7ba5e.

The mistake came from where I saw the id: the 2023 entry is a "Document Link" item, aabc6d4751614c479d51ff607c6ee1d4, titled "AK Game Mgmt Units (eff 7/1/2023) (link)", and ITS url field points at the 2025 item. So following the 2023 link lands on 2025 terms while the 2023 item's own licenceInfo still states the 2023 ones — two editions reachable through one link, disagreeing about both the scale ceiling and the prohibition's scope.

HOW THE ID WAS VERIFIED, since a title is not evidence: by matching each item's own licenceInfo against the text recorded in `statedAs`. f1019b… mentions 1:63,360 and "Users may not reproduce"; aabc6d… mentions 1:250,000 and "3rd-party". The id is therefore confirmed by the words it carries rather than by the label on it.

Resolving a hunter's GPS position to the unit they are standing in is precisely using this data with GPS to determine a physical boundary. So even if consent to redistribute were granted, this layer could not answer "which unit am I in" on ADF&G's own terms.
theTermsAlsoForbidTheUseHuntMakes.whyItIsRecordedSeparatelyFromTheLicence: Because the two are undone by different things. Consent would answer the redistribution clause and leave this one standing. Recording it inside the licence note would let a future reader who obtains consent conclude the state is unblocked.
theTermsAlsoForbidTheUseHuntMakes.notTheSameAsTheUsualCaveat: §41 already requires that consumer GPS is never presented as a legal survey, and every authority disclaims accuracy. This is stronger and rarer: the publisher naming the operation and forbidding it. Alaska is the first US state found to do so.

geography.term: Deer Management Zone (DMZ)
geography.definedBy: NJDEP Division of Fish and Wildlife's own published zones, Edition 20200901
geography.theNamedLayerIsTheWrongCONCEPT:
The trap here is not an inflated count — it is a layer with a plausible name that is a DIFFERENT KIND OF THING. New Jersey publishes both:
  Deer Management ZONES  —  88 polygons, the season-setting geography.
  Deer Management UNITS  — 632 polygons, field DMU, values a sequential 1..632.
632 sequential integers is a fine analysis grid, not a regulatory unit system. My first pass recorded New Jersey as "632 Deer Management Units" on the strength of the layer's name, which would have served a grid cell where the rule uses a zone — a wrong answer carrying a real-looking unit id. Distinguishing them needed the DISTINCT values of the unit field, not the feature count: the count is identical either way.

geography.term: deer hunting Zone (Zones 1–4); separately an elk restoration zone subdivided into Elk Hunting Units
geography.definedBy: 301 KAR 2:172, "Deer hunting seasons, zones, and requirements", in force, HISTORY terminating "52 Ky.R. 479; eff. 3-3-2026". The zones are NOT polygons: the regulation enumerates every county by name into a zone, exhaustively and without overlap — 68 + 24 + 13 + 15 = 120, which is exactly Kentucky's county count. No geographic inference is required to build them.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The deer layer returns 120 features. That is a COUNTY count, not a zone count: the unit count is 4. Elk is worse in both directions — "Elk Management Zones" returns 16 features that are 16 COUNTIES comprising ONE zone, while Elk Hunting Units returns 6 features that really are 6 units, numbered 2 to 7 with NO UNIT 1, so a consumer assuming 1–6 would mis-key every one. "Elk Restricted Hunting Areas" returns 252 features that are not 252 prohibitions.

THE CLEAREST UNITED STATES PERMISSION FOUND. An affirmative CC0 1.0 dedication, and unlike Hawaii it carries no unresolvable carve-out: the portal item's licenseInfo links creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/ and the KyGovMaps DCAT-US catalog independently states license "https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0" for every KDFWR hunting dataset, with rights null. The rest is a warranty disclaimer, which is not a refusal. One item (Elk Hunting Units) prefixes it with "No limits, credit KDFWR" — an attribution condition and an express statement of no limits, and it is read onto that item only, not across the others.

SERVICE-LEVEL copyrightText IS AN EMPTY STRING on every KDFWR layer checked, so reading the service alone would have produced "no terms stated" on the one state with the best terms in the country.

THE TERMS PAGE WAS NOT ESTABLISHED, and the control is why. kygeonet.ky.gov/terms and technology.ky.gov/gis/Pages/Disclaimer.aspx both 404. opengisdata.ky.gov/pages/terms-of-use returns 200 — but so does a deliberately bogus path on the same host, at nearly identical size, because the site is a single-page app that answers 200 for anything. That 200 is not evidence a terms page exists, and none is reported.

lawVersusGis.finding: THE MOST DANGEROUS FINDING OF THE UNITED STATES SWEEP. KDFWR's own deer-zone layer assigns 46 of Kentucky's 120 counties to a different zone than the law in force. Both publications partition all 120 counties and their county universes are identical, so this is not a coverage artefact — it is a substantive disagreement about zone membership. Adair 1→2, Bath 2→3, Jackson 3→4, Knox 4→3, Pike 3→4, Whitley 4→3, Pulaski 3→4, Madison 2→3, among others.
lawVersusGis.lawSays: 301 KAR 2:172, eff. 3-3-2026 — Zone 1: 68 counties, Zone 2: 24, Zone 3: 13, Zone 4: 15. Sum 120.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: KDFWR "Annual Deer Management Zones in Kentucky", field CURRENTZONE — Zone 1: 40, Zone 2: 43, Zone 3: 19, Zone 4: 18. Sum 120.
lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: Not asserted — measured. CURRENTZONE is byte-identical to the same layer's own DZ200708 column across all 120 features: `where=CURRENTZONE<>DZ200708&returnCountOnly=true` returns 0, against a positive control of `where=CURRENTZONE>0` returning 120 on the same layer by the same method. The column aliased "Current Years Deer Zone" is the 2007-08 season, about 19 years stale. The alternatives were ruled out rather than assumed: it matches neither the proposed successor 301 KAR 2:172REG (also 68/24/13/15) nor the immediately prior edition eff. 6-18-2025 (51/35/12/22), so it is neither ahead of the law nor one edition behind — it matches no edition reachable. A third publication breaks the tie: the 2026-27 guide's bag limits match the in-force KAR exactly, and its zone-map legend includes a "Zone change" category, which a layer frozen at 2007-08 cannot express.
lawVersusGis.everySurfaceSignalSaidCurrent: Right publisher, "Annual" in the title, the column aliased "Current Years Deer Zone", lastEditDate and dataLastEditDate 2026-07-10, portal modified 2026-07-10, 120 clean county polygons, exactly four zone values. And the licence is CC0, so no licence check would have stopped it. A clear licence over stale data is more dangerous than a refusal, because a refusal stops you.
lawVersusGis.doNotServe: Do NOT serve CURRENTZONE. Ingesting it would have shipped a plausible, official-looking, KDFWR-published deer-zone map that misstates the zone — and therefore the antlerless bag limit — for 38% of Kentucky. The layer's dated DZ* columns remain legitimate as historical evidence, labelled by their own year.
lawVersusGis.servablePathFromTheLaw: Kentucky IS servable, from the law rather than from the layer: join 301 KAR 2:172's county enumeration to Ky_County_Polygons_WM (CC0). The join matches 120 of 120 counties with zero unmatched names in either direction. Two normalisations are required and neither is a judgement call — they are typographical errors in the regulation itself: it spells "McClean" for McLean and "Elliot" for Elliott.

geography.term: Deer Management Unit (DMU), within Zone
geography.definedBy: Rule 68A-13.0001, F.A.C., "Definitions", effective 7/1/2026. Subsection (1)(a)–(l) defines TWELVE DMUs — A1, A2, A3, B1, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, D1, D2 — each as "That portion of Zone [X] located …"; subsection (2)(a)–(d) defines FOUR Zones by county, with many counties split by road or water descriptions.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: For the DMU layer they AGREE, and that is worth recording because it is the only clean 1:1 layer found in the United States: 12 features, 12 distinct DMU values, 12 codified units, each DMU in exactly one feature, no status field, no region field, no closures, nothing mixed in. The WMA layer is the opposite — 284 features, 160 distinct NAME, 154 among the four hunting-area types, so it overstates by 124. Fifteen features are not hunting-area types at all (2 Air Force Base, 1 Air Force Range, 1 Preserve, 11 Public Use Area) and 121 features carry a UNIT value, meaning one named area is split across several polygons. TYPE_SHORT is not a usable key: "WMA" maps to BOTH "Wildlife Management Area" and "Waterfowl Management Area".
geography.theLayerStopsShortOfTheLaw: The DMU layer's southern limit is ymin 24.8814°N, and Rule 68A-13.0001(2)(a) places the whole of Monroe County — the Florida Keys — in Zone A. Point queries: Key Largo (25.10, -80.44) returns A1/Zone A; Marathon (24.71, -81.09) returns ZERO features; Big Pine Key (24.68, -81.35) returns ZERO. Both misses persisted with tolerance — Big Pine at 10 km and Marathon at 30 km — so this is a layer that stops, not a point that fell in water between islands. FWC's OTHER hunting layer contradicts that limit: the WMA service contains "Florida Keys Wildlife and Environmental Area" with ymin 24.5770°N, about 34 km further south. §8 in both directions: a Keys point below 24.8814°N must not be given an invented DMU, must NOT be reported closed or zoneless when the rule text plainly places it in Zone A, and the mainland must not be discarded because the lower Keys are unresolvable.

licence.statedAs: Users are encouraged to read and fully comprehend the metadata record prior to using these data. Please acknowledge the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) as the data source for any products developed from these data. FWC shall not be liable for improper or incorrect use of these data.

licence.note:
PERMITTED WITH REAL CONDITIONS, and the grant is in a THIRD instrument the second one incorporates by reference. The portal item says "Users are encouraged to read and fully comprehend the metadata record prior to using these data" — and the FGDC metadata record is where the reuse position actually is. Verbatim from it: “This data set is in the public domain, and the recipient may not assert any proprietary rights thereto nor represent it to anyone as other than a Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission produced data set. These data are unrestricted. Where possible, always acquire this dataset directly from FWC as other sources may have altered the original data. FWRI-DC Available without restriction. Metadata must be distributed with the data set.” Read independently on all three datasets (DMU 46,605 bytes; WMA 167,163; BMU 47,600), with the BMU record putting the same language in <useconst>/<accconst> where the others use <useLimit>/<resConst>.

FOUR CONDITIONS THAT ARE OBLIGATIONS, not caveats to drop: acknowledge FWC as the data source in any product developed from the data; do not assert proprietary rights; do not represent it as other than FWC-produced; and DISTRIBUTE THE METADATA WITH THE DATA SET. The last is the one a normal implementation silently breaks.

Service-level copyrightText is NOT empty here, breaking the usual pattern — but it is an attribution string and states no terms, so it is not the instrument either. The agency's own terms page does not exist: four candidate URLs 404 or return an empty Hub shell, and an enumeration of FWC's ten Hub pages lists no terms page.

separateInstrumentNotMerged.artifact: the annual regulations brochure at eregulations.com
separateInstrumentNotMerged.finding: Hosted by a COMMERCIAL PUBLISHER, not FWC, and the FWC GIS terms say nothing about it. Its reuse position is UNKNOWN and was not established. This blocks nothing: the underlying rules are in the Florida Administrative Code on flrules.org and can be encoded as structured facts in North Ground's own words with the rule cited, which is exactly what §8's "the law's answer, not a copy of the law's prose" provides for.

lawVersusGis.finding: FWC's deer geography stops 34 km north of FWC's own southernmost hunting area, and both stop north of where the rule reaches.
lawVersusGis.lawSays: Rule 68A-13.0001(2)(a) places all of Monroe County in Zone A, and every DMU is a portion of a Zone.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: DMU layer southern limit 24.8814°N; WMA layer southern limit 24.5770°N (Florida Keys WEA).
lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: Queried extents in EPSG:4326 with returnExtentOnly, plus three point queries and two tolerance retries at 10 km and 30 km. No FWC statement explaining the exclusion was found.
lawVersusGis.doNotServe: The mainland and upper Keys ARE servable and must not be discarded. Below 24.8814°N do not give a point a DMU, and do not report it as no-zone or closed — it is an unresolved point inside a zone the law names. Florida's DMU layer is otherwise the only exact 1:1 match with a codified unit list found in the United States.
lawVersusGis.servablePathFromTheLaw: None for the lower Keys as geometry: Rule 68A-13.0001(2)(a) names Monroe County in full, so the zone MEMBERSHIP is known from the text even where the polygon stops — which is enough to say a Keys point is in Zone A, and not enough to say which DMU within it.

geography.term: Zone, per species — Arkansas has no single statewide unit system and the zone sets do not nest
geography.definedBy: The AGFC Code of Regulations. Chapter 02.00 "Zone Regulations" was read directly rather than inferred from its title, and it does NOT contain the deer, bear or turkey zone boundaries — those sit in the Code Addendum chapters with the zone maps published in the annual guidebook.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: Deer 20 features = 20 distinct labels = 20 guidebook zones: MATCH. Bear 8 = 8: MATCH, at LAYER ID 4, not 0. Alligator 5 at layer 3. CWD 1 at layer 5. But WMA fires the trap twice: WMABoundaries layer 13 returns 139 features for 138 distinct names, and AGFC_Wildlife_Management_Areas_WV returns 192 features for the same 138 — the extra 54 are OWNERSHIP PARCELS inside WMAs, not units. Turkey (5 units) and elk (4 units) have NO published GIS at all, and Elk_Range is not a substitute: its own serviceDescription reads "Elk range as provided by Mr. Watt at UAM Monticello" — a third-party range polygon, not a regulatory boundary.

licence.statedAs: This feature layer was produced by AGFC GIS staff to visualize general location(s) of subject property. Unless otherwise stated, features depicted herein do not represent legal or survey boundaries and are intended for reference purposes only.
licence.attribution: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission
licence.note:
THE LICENCE FIELD IS NOT WHERE THE RESTRICTION IS, and this is the state that proves reading it alone produces a false green light. `licenseInfo` — recorded above as `statedAs` — is a boundary-accuracy disclaimer and would block NOTHING on its own. The express limitation of permitted use is in the portal item's `description`: see `termsInTheDescriptionField`. Service-level and layer-level copyrightText are the empty string on every AGFC hunting layer.

The agency's /acceptable-use/ page grants no data reuse and prohibits only website framing ("You may not capture Arkansas.gov pages within frames or present Arkansas.gov content as your own"). The one WMA layer lacking the restriction sentence (AGFC_Wildlife_Management_Areas_WV) states nothing on any of the three instruments, and silence is not a grant. So nothing AGFC publishes grants reuse.

termsInTheDescriptionField.statedAs: This feature layer is intended for educational purposes only and is not for use beyond AGFC's Generation Conservation Summit. Data in this feature layer is accurate as of 2025-08-11. Any changes to AGFC's deer zones after 2025-08-11 will not be reflected in this feature layer.
termsInTheDescriptionField.whyItMatters: "is not for use beyond AGFC's Generation Conservation Summit" limits permitted use to ONE INTERNAL AGFC EVENT. For a public product that is a refusal — not an attribution condition, not an indemnity, not an accuracy caveat. The same sentence appears on the bear, alligator, CWD and WMA items with the species word swapped, so it is the account's standard text rather than one layer's slip.
termsInTheDescriptionField.whatTheLicenceFieldSaidInstead: An accuracy disclaimer: features "do not represent legal or survey boundaries and are intended for reference purposes only". Recording that as the terms would have cleared Arkansas.

findings.note: The restriction is a scope limit on those PUBLISHED ARTEFACTS, not a copyright claim over the underlying facts. The zone identities — 20 deer zones, 8 bear zones, 5 turkey zones — are facts stated in the Code and the guidebook and may be encoded in North Ground's own words under §8. What cannot be used is AGFC's geometry.

geography.term: Indiana has NO single named hunting-unit system: County for deer bag limits, Deer Reduction Zone, and Waterfowl Hunting Zone are three different geographies with three different legal terms
geography.definedBy: the portal item's own metes-and-bounds description ("North: That part of Indiana north of a line extending east from the Illinois border along State Road 18 to U.S. 31…")
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: Counties 92 = 92: match. Waterfowl zones 3 = 3: match. But Deer Reduction Zones return 34 features for only 18 distinct NAMED zones — 15 features carry a BLANK `Area` (verified: `where=Area='  '&returnCountOnly=true` returns 15) — so 34 overstates by about 1.9x, and the fields `unitname` and `SymbolID` are entirely blank and unusable as keys. The service name "Traditional & Corridors" explains it: one named zone carries a traditional polygon plus corridor polygons. Public hunting properties: 190 features, 120 distinct properties, at LAYER ID 1 — layer 0 does not exist on that service.

licence.statedAs: DATA DISCLAIMER: This item, including its underlying data, is restricted for use by the Indiana Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) Division of Fish & Wildlife and approved partners only.
licence.attribution: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Fish & Wildlife
licence.note:
AN EXPRESS RESTRICTION ON WHO MAY USE THE DATA, and it lands on the one layer that matters. North Ground is not an "approved partner". It is not cured by the item being access:public or by the word "Public" in its title. Indiana's ONLY genuine regulatory-zone vector layer — 3 features, 3 units, clean, current — is the one we may not use.

ONE AGENCY, TWO DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS. The county bag-limit, Deer Reduction Zone, CWD and deer-density items carry a DIFFERENT licenseInfo that is warranty and liability language only, with no refusal. So Indiana cannot be classified from one item; the restriction must be read per dataset.

Service-level copyrightText is an empty string on all thirteen Indiana services checked, with a positive control (USGS basemap) confirming the reader surfaces real copyrightText when present — so the emptiness is Indiana's, not the method's. Reading only the service would have concluded everything was free to use.

This is NOT a §8 reproduction-licence question that can be routed around by re-expressing the rule in our own words: the restriction is on USING THE DATA, and the data here is geometry, not prose. The zone DEFINITIONS are published as metes-and-bounds text in the item description and could in principle be encoded independently — that route is untested and would need its own authorization.

lawVersusGis.finding: A layer titled "Active CWD Indiana Counties upd. 05/2026" and described as "all Indiana counties that are active CWD zones as of 05/2026" CONTAINS ALL 92 COUNTIES — i.e. it asserts the entire state is an active CWD zone.
lawVersusGis.lawSays: The same author's companion item, "CWD Positive Townships upd. 05/2026", holds 5 positive townships.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: 92 of 92 counties, at layer 105 of CWD_CountyZones_2024_ExportFeatures.
lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: Feature count 92 against Indiana's 92 counties, beside the same owner's 5-feature positive-township layer at layer 104. Both items are owned by JCaudell@dnr.IN.gov_indnr and modified 2026-05-07.
lawVersusGis.doNotServe: Do not serve the county CWD layer as a restriction geography. Drawing it would place every Indiana hunter inside a disease-management zone, which is the loose-direction failure §8 forbids just as firmly as the strict one.

speciesHeatCandidate.finding: 9,318 one-square-mile cells of estimated deer density — the best US deer-abundance evidence found so far, at LAYER ID 132. Relevant to §41B rather than to the map lane, and subject to the same instrument question: it carries Indiana's conditions-only licenseInfo, not the waterfowl refusal.
speciesHeatCandidate.doNotActOnItYet: §41B requires a declared resolution, evidence class, methodology and confidence before any surface is drawn. None of that is established here.

geography.term: Deer Season Zone (A–E), Turkey Season Zone (1–3), dove North/South Zone, CWD Management Zone with High-Risk and Buffer Zones, Mobile-Tensaw Delta Waterfowl Management Zone, five Alligator Management Areas
geography.definedBy: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.01 and r. 220-2-.77, Agency 220 Chapter 220-2 "Game And Fish Division". Deer Zones A–E are defined ONLY as narrative metes-and-bounds along highways, rivers, bypasses and county lines — Zone A's description alone runs about 2,300 characters — and Zones B–E are partly defined by EXCLUSION ("Excludes Zones C, D, and E").
geography.theAbsenceIsTheFinding:
THE SPECIES-DETERMINATIVE GEOGRAPHY IS NOT PUBLISHED AS VECTOR DATA BY ANYONE. ADCNR's own ArcGIS Server has 46 services and not one is a zone layer — confirmed from the authoritative directory listing and by probing DeerZones, HuntingZones, TurkeyZones, Zones and CWD, each of which returns HTTP 200 carrying {"error":{"code":404,"message":"Service not found"}}. A point therefore CANNOT be resolved to an Alabama deer zone. Deriving those lines ourselves from highway centrelines, river courses and bypass alignments would be North Ground inventing a regulatory boundary, which §41A forbids outright. Deer — Alabama's most-hunted species — is unserviceable at point resolution, and that is a genuine evidentiary gap, not an implementation limitation.

Turkey and dove are different: those zones are COUNTY LISTS (turkey Zone 1 = 44 counties, Zone 2 = 9, Zone 3 = 6; dove South = 9 named counties, North = all others), and ADCNR publishes 67 county polygons. One county is split by text ("Cullman (except north of Lewis Smith Lake and north of Cullman County Road 437 and west of I-65)"), so turkey is resolvable for 66 counties and unresolved inside Cullman.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The 42-feature "WildlifeManagementAreas" layer is not 42 WMAs. By name suffix it holds 29 WMA, 4 Tract, 3 Management Area, 2 NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE (federal: Cahaba River, Key Cave), 2 Refuge and 2 Community Hunting Area — and the layer carries NO class or status field, so class is recoverable only by parsing the name string. Three features are absent from r. 220-2-.22 entirely (Dutch Bend, Jacinto Port and Tom Roush Tracts), and the layer calls "Grand Bay Savanna" a Wildlife Management Area where the rule establishes it as a Community Hunting Area. The SOA layer's 15 exceeds the rule's 13.
geography.theLegalBoundaryIsElsewhere: r. 220-2-.22(1) fixes it expressly: "The boundary lines of these areas and refuges shall be as they are described on the maps attached in Chapter 220-2-A Appendix A." The GIS layer is therefore not the legal boundary instrument even for the areas it does cover.

licenceAbsent.finding: No instrument reachable states any reuse, redistribution, attribution or derived-product term for Alabama's hunting geography — and none states a prohibition either. Service-level copyrightText is the empty string at both MapServer and layer level on all five hunting-relevant services, and serviceDescription and description are empty too. There is NO ARCGIS PORTAL ITEM AT ALL, so the instrument that carried the terms in Kentucky, Arkansas, Indiana, Pennsylvania and New Jersey does not exist here.
whereLooked: service copyrightText at MapServer and layer level, five services
ArcGIS portal item licenseInfo — no portal item exists
licenceAbsent.controlForTheAbsence: The same reader surfaces real copyrightText elsewhere in the same sweep (Florida's is a non-empty attribution string, Washington's lines item carries a full caveat), so the emptiness is Alabama's and not the method's.
licenceAbsent.whatWouldUnblockIt: ADCNR stating terms for its GIS, which is the owner's to ask.
licenceAbsent.whyItsOwnStateAndNotReachability: Every service answered 200. Nothing is unreachable; nothing is stated.

conflict.finding: Two ADCNR publications disagree about the extent of the CWD Management Zone. The codified rule, r. 220-2-.01(1)(f)6 effective 5 June 2026, read in both the HTML render and independently in the rule PDF: "The CWD Management Zone (CMZ) includes all of Lauderdale, Colbert, and Franklin Counties" — THREE whole counties. The agency's own outdooralabama.com page states a different extent.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: The codified rule is the instrument and would normally govern, but the CMZ contains a High-Risk Zone and a Buffer Zone whose boundaries are also narrative, and no vector geometry exists for any of them — so there is nothing to serve either way. Recording the disagreement is the whole available action.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: ADCNR reconciling its web page with r. 220-2-.01(1)(f)6, or publishing the CMZ as geometry.

legalHours.finding: A THIRD KIND OF HOURS RULE, and the inverse of Washington and Pennsylvania. Not a table dressed as a formula — a term with NO FORMULA AT ALL. Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.05, "Legal Hunting Hours For Game Birds": "Legal hunting hours for game birds during the open season shall be daylight hours only, except as otherwise provided by law or regulation." "Daylight hours" is UNDEFINED in the rule. North Ground's astronomy cannot reproduce it because there is no numeric rule to reproduce, and choosing an offset would be inventing the law. Alabama then layers computable solar offsets and fixed civil clock times onto specific species and geographies.
legalHours.contrastWithKentucky: Kentucky states the same phrase and DEFINES it: KRS 150.010(8), "'Daylight hours' means the period from one-half (1/2) hour before sunrise to one-half (1/2) hour after sunset." So the identical words are certifiable in one state and not in the other, and the difference is a statutory definition. Carrying Kentucky's definition into Alabama would be the exact error §8 forbids.

geography.term: per-species/per-season Zone (IDNR has no umbrella term); COUNTY for deer
geography.definedBy: 17 Ill. Adm. Code Part 530 (cock pheasant, Hungarian partridge, bobwhite quail, rabbit) and Part 590 (duck, goose and coot), plus the turkey and furbearer Parts, each implementing the Wildlife Code, 520 ILCS 5. For deer, 17 Ill. Adm. Code 650.10(b): "Permit quotas shall be set by the Department of Natural Resources on a county or special hunt area basis."
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The error runs BOTH ways here. 15 features across 5 distinct Species values (Bobcat, Furbearer, Turkey, Upland Game, Waterfowl) — so 15 is not a count of one system's units, and a point query at Springfield returns SIX overlapping features, because the zone sets of different species overlay each other. And DEER, Illinois' highest-demand species, does not appear in the layer at all.

lawVersusGis.lawSays: IDNR's own release, "IDNR announces waterfowl season dates and zone lines for 2026-2030", dated 21 October 2025: "Since 2011, Illinois has had four waterfowl hunting zones without split duck seasons", and for 2026-2030 "the former South-Central and South zones have been combined to form one South Zone" — THREE zones.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: Layer 4 still carries "South Central Duck & Goose Zone" alongside North, Central and South — FOUR zones.
lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: The abolishing publication is the authority's own, dated, and names the combination explicitly; the layer's Zone values still list the abolished zone.
lawVersusGis.everySurfaceSignalSaidCurrent: A 200 from IDNR's own host, resolving points live in WGS84, returning clean named zones.

geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 86 features, and neither 86 nor the 74 distinct attribute combinations is a unit count. 81 features form a single statewide tessellation — proven by area arithmetic, not by assumption: sum(Shape__Area) where NR_Deer IS NOT NULL is 145,581 km² against Iowa's ~145,746 km², n=81. The other 5 are an OVERLAY, not units: they are the only rows where every species field is NULL, they carry the field aliased "Closed Canada Goose Area", and their envelopes are five small areas totalling about 109 km² near Oelwein, Bellevue, Lake Panorama, Creston and Winterset. Counting them as zones is exactly the trap.

conflict.finding: Resident Fall Turkey Zone 9 is quota'd and mapped but never defined in text. IAC 571—98.2(3) sets fall resident quotas for SIX zones ("a. Zone 4: 1,500. b. Zone 5: 650. c. Zone 6: 1,400. d. Zone 7: 250. e. Zone 8: 200. f. Zone 9: 200."), while IAC 571—98.10 "Zones open to hunting" defines only FIVE zones textually — 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, by highways. The GIS layer carries six distinct values, 4 to 9, with 12 polygons at Zone 9, and the booklet's printed map shows a 9. So Zone 9 exists in three of the authority's publications and in none of its boundary definitions.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: A quota and a map label are not a boundary definition. Serving Zone 9's polygons would assert a boundary the rule that opens the zone does not state; refusing all six would discard five zones that ARE defined, which §8 forbids.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: IAC 571—98.10 being amended to define Zone 9, or the incorporated-by-reference map being identified for it.

findings.note: A PREDICTION THAT WAS WRONG, recorded because it changes the verdict. I expected Iowa to be county-only geography with no zone service, and the atlas layer to hold about 99 county polygons. Both were wrong in the same direction: Iowa publishes a genuine multi-species zone layer tiling into 81 units. Iowa is MORE servable than expected, not less, and the only thing standing in the way is that its terms are unstated.

geography.term: NONE — no hunting management geography exists in the District
geography.definedBy: The absence of an instrument, established affirmatively rather than inferred. D.C. Official Code Title 8 Ch. 22 Subch. II and its criminal-code parallel Title 22 Ch. 43 show §§ .01–.27 marked [Repealed] or [Transferred] — including "Killing game birds and permits therefor", "Hunting squirrels, chipmunks and rabbits without a permit" and "Hunting or disbursing of ducks, geese, and waterfowl". Only the authority and enforcement sections survive. What replaced them is one blanket protection, 19 DCMR § 1560.1: "All wildlife in the District is protected, and none shall be killed or otherwise taken except in accordance with this chapter" — and the chapter authorises no taking, so it is a closed loop with nothing in it.
geography.theAbsenceIsTheFinding:
WHAT DC LACKS IS HUNTING, NOT DATA, and that distinction is the whole finding. Unit count 0; the nearest available geography is the District boundary, one polygon, whose identifying fields are CITY_NAME and STATE_CITY — a city identifier, not a unit id. Enumerating a unit field is moot because there is none.

READ FAR ENOUGH TO BE SURE, WITH A POSITIVE CONTROL IN THE SAME LISTING. The whole of DCMR chapter 19-15 was enumerated from the official rule list: 35 sections, of which 19-1500 to 19-1508 are FISHING, 19-1520 to 19-1530 urban apiculture, 19-1565 to 19-1579 wildlife rehabilitation and nuisance-wildlife control, 19-1599 definitions, and 19-1560 the only hunting section. There is no hunting season, licence, bag limit, method or hours section anywhere. The control is built into the same listing: it DOES return 19-1504 species minimum size and possession limits, 19-1505 licence fees and 19-1506 fishing seasons — so the listing is complete and the fetcher works, and the hunting provisions are genuinely absent rather than missed.
geography.theFederalRouteIsClosedToo:
The one vehicle by which a DC season with hours could otherwise exist. 50 CFR 20.100(a) prohibits migratory game bird hunting except as authorized for State and Tribal regulations, and 50 CFR 20.107 defines the flyways exhaustively — the Atlantic Flyway is enumerated and the District of Columbia is not in it, nor in any other. Across all of part 20 "District of Columbia" occurs exactly twice, both inside the § 20.11 definition of "Resident Canada geese", never as a hunting jurisdiction. Positive controls on the same text: Maryland 2, Virginia 2, Pennsylvania 2, New Jersey 2, "Atlantic Flyway" 4. Separately 50 CFR 80.2 states that "State" includes DC for the Sport Fish Restoration Act and does NOT include it for the Wildlife Restoration Act — DC is a Dingell-Johnson jurisdiction and not a Pittman-Robertson one.

AND AN INDEPENDENT DISTRICT BLOCKER: D.C. Official Code § 22-4503.01 — "no firearm shall be discharged or set off in the District of Columbia without a special written permit from the Chief of Police", with only two exceptions, discharges "otherwise permitted by law" and "legitimate self-defense". No hunting exception.

completableNow.finding: THE FIRST UNITED STATES JURISDICTION THAT CAN BE FINISHED. DC is servable today as a single certified jurisdiction-wide CLOSED answer: no geography problem, no licence problem, no ambiguity. Everything needed is a structured fact in North Ground's own words — all wildlife protected, no season for any species, no hunting licence issued, no hunting units — citing 19 DCMR § 1560.1, D.C. Official Code § 8-2221.28 and § 22-4503.01, and 50 CFR 20.100(a) and 20.107. The only verbatim retention warranted is § 1560.1 itself, whose scope turns on its wording.
completableNow.whyItMustNotBeServedAsUNKNOWN: The absence of a season here is AFFIRMATIVELY ESTABLISHED, not merely unfound. Reporting DC as UNKNOWN or unserviceable would understate what the authority establishes, which §8 treats as the same class of error as overstating it. This is the clearest available case of the under-claim direction that §8 says nobody ever reports.
completableNow.hours: There are no legal hunting hours in the District, and that too is a finding rather than a default: not a solar offset, not a published table, and not unknown. No hours rule exists because no season exists to attach one to. No species is singled out; the only species named in the chapter's take provisions are "rats, mice, moles and other depredating wildlife" under the § 1560.2 property-protection exception, which carries no hours, season or bag limit.

boundaryFidelityIsTheBlocker.statedAs: Hunt boundary shown is an approximation. Hunters are responsible for knowing the exact boundary locations as described within Section 360, Title 14, Calif. Code of Regs.
boundaryFidelityIsTheBlocker.finding: A licence that permits use is not a layer that can place a point. California's own words put the legal boundary in §360's text and its polygon in the position of an estimate — which is the DERIVED_FROM_LEGAL_DESCRIPTION pattern, and it means a near-boundary answer must carry that limit explicitly.
boundaryFidelityIsTheBlocker.separateFromTheLicence: A grant and a fidelity disclaimer are different facts; merging them would either block a permitted state or serve an approximation as a boundary.

geography.definedBy: CT DEEP's own published zones; the agency's 2026 Deer Hunting page states "4 of Connecticut's 13 deer management zones", which corroborates the count from its own prose

I predicted "12 zones plus one multipart duplicate"; the truth is 13 distinct values with zero duplicates — 1, 2, 3, 4a, 4b, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 — because Zone 4 is genuinely SUBDIVIDED into 4A and 4B and both are rule-bearing: DEEP's antlerless restriction reads "Statewide (except Zones 2 and 4A)" and "Zones 2 and 4A: 1 either sex". Treating 4A as a cartographic split would have dropped a regulatory unit. Geometry is clean: 13 single-part polygons, 17,888 vertices, native EPSG:2234, served in 4326 on request; the area sum of 12,874 km² against Connecticut's 12,542 km² land and 14,357 km² land-plus-water rules out gross overlap while showing modest coastal-water inclusion.

On STATE land, hunting is governed by DEEP's hunting-area and lottery system rather than by zone. So a correct zone answer on state land is answering the wrong question, and the boundaries follow town lines.

A THIRD typo survives in both: Zone 14 reads "north by Route 9, south by Route 24, east by Route 113, and south by Route 24" — "south" twice and no western bound — so Zone 14's published prose description is internally incomplete even though its polygon is present.

theCwdZoneIsDerivable.finding: DNREC's 2026/27 addendum: "We have designated a CWD Management Zone (CMZ) for disease management, made up of Wildlife Management Zones 11, 14 and 16", with baiting prohibited inside it, mandatory 24-hour check-in during the Nov 13–22 General Firearm season, and carcass bagging requirements.
theCwdZoneIsDerivable.whyItMatters: The CMZ has NO polygon of its own — it is exactly the union of three certified WMZ polygons, so it is derivable deterministically from the layer rather than being a missing geography. That is the opposite of Alabama's CWD zone, which is narrative prose with nothing to derive it from.
theCwdZoneIsDerivable.theOneZoneScopedSeason: Delaware is overwhelmingly a statewide-season state: every deer season row reads "Statewide" except one — "Handgun and Straight-walled Pistol-caliber Rifle | Season closed in Wildlife Management Zones 1A and 1B | Jan. 2–10". That single line is the whole coordinate→zone→rule dependency for Delaware deer seasons, and it is real.

geography.term: Deer Management Unit (DMU)
geography.definedBy: 40 Miss. Admin. Code, Part 2 (Wildlife), Chapter 2, Rule 2.2 "2026-27 Deer Seasons and Bag Limits" (rev. 04-2026 FINAL). Each DMU is defined by highways or whole counties: Delta — "Areas west of I-55 and north of I-20 plus areas south of I-20 and west of U.S. Highway 61"; Southeast — "Areas south of U.S. Highway 84 and east of MS Highway 35"; North Central — "All portions of Alcorn, Benton, Desoto, Marshall, Tate, and Tippah counties"; and Hills as the RESIDUAL — "All areas except the Delta, North Central, and Southeast Deer Management Units."
geography.theNameMismatchWouldBreakAResolver:
The layer's Name values are NORTH EAST ZONE, DELTA ZONE, SOUTH ZONE and NORTH CENTRAL ZONE, and TWO OF THE FOUR do not match the regulatory unit names: "NORTH EAST ZONE" against "Hills Unit", and "SOUTH ZONE" against "Southeast Unit". The non-contiguous labels 10, 12, 13, 15 are the signature of a legacy classification that once had more members.

So the correspondence was established by SEVENTEEN point-in-polygon queries against the live layer rather than by joining on name, and every one agreed with Rule 2.2: Corinth and Senatobia → NORTH CENTRAL; Greenville and Rolling Fork → DELTA; Pascagoula and Bay St. Louis → SOUTH; Tishomingo, Meridian, Pontotoc, Grenada, Laurel, McComb, Tylertown and a point southwest of I-20 east of US 61 → NORTH EAST. No point returned two features, and a simply-connected concave residual is consistent with the Hills definition.

BUT THE CROSSWALK IS OURS, NOT THE AUTHORITY'S. The layer carries no regulatory unit name and no crosswalk, and Id, ACRES and REFERENCE are dead fields. The mapping is well supported by our testing and is NOT published, so it must be recorded as North Ground's derivation rather than as the authority's.

rulesHostTlsProblem.finding: mdwfp.com does not serve its intermediate certificate. Node's fetch rejects it with "unable to verify the first certificate"; curl and browsers accept it — the same URL returns HTTP 200 with 268,866 bytes to curl, over both HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1, with ssl_verify_result 0.
rulesHostTlsProblem.whyItIsNotRecordedAsABLOCKER: Because it is not one, and recording it as one would have invented a blocker for a state whose site works. My own source-URL checker reported Mississippi UNREACHABLE on its first run, because `fetch` describes every transport failure as the same useless string, "fetch failed". Unwrapping error.cause is what distinguished an incomplete chain from a refusal. The checker now classifies the cause and says in its output that a TLS finding must be confirmed with a second client before anything is recorded.
rulesHostTlsProblem.howItDiffersFromArizona: Arizona is TRANSPORT_BLOCKED for an EXPIRED certificate — expired since 2022, which no client should accept. An incomplete chain is a weaker and far more common misconfiguration: the certificate is valid and the server simply omits a link, so most clients reconstruct it and succeed. Treating the two alike would overstate Mississippi and understate Arizona.
rulesHostTlsProblem.consequenceForIngestion: Any North Ground fetcher built on Node's fetch will fail against mdwfp.com and must either supply the intermediate or use a client that completes the chain. That is an implementation note, not a coverage limit, and Mississippi's real position is unchanged: servable geography, unstated terms.

geography.term: COUNTY — there is no North Carolina hunting "zone" in any legal instrument
geography.definedBy: 15A NCAC 10B .0203(a)(1)(A)–(E) for deer and .0202(a)(1)–(8) for bear, both of which ENUMERATE COUNTIES and use no zone name at all. The names "NORTHEASTERN", "SOUTHEASTERN", "CENTRAL", "NORTHWESTERN", "WESTERN" and the three Bear Management Units appear ONLY in NCWRC's published one-page season-dates sheet — so the zone is a PRESENTATION LABEL over a county list, not a regulatory geography. CWD is the exception and IS defined in rule: 15A NCAC 10B .0501(b)(4)–(9) and .0502(a).
geography.theCountyListsReconcileExactly: Checked rather than trusted: .0203(a)(1)(A)=23 counties, (B)=22, (C)=12, (D)=17, (E)=19, totalling 93; 10B .0502(a) names the remaining 7 (Cumberland, Forsyth, Sampson, Stokes, Surry, Wilkes, Yadkin); 93+7=100, which is North Carolina's county count. And each of the five presentation zones' county lists matches its codified paragraph county-for-county.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: nc_counties_view is a clean 100 features / 100 distinct CO_NAME. CountyBoundaryShoreline returns 127 FEATURES for the same 100 distinct NAME and FIPS — the 27 extra are land and water shoreline splits, distinguishable by a WATER field whose distinct values are 'A' and 'S'. Using that layer's count would overstate the unit system by 27.
geography.districtIsNotAUnit: NCWRC "District" 1–9 is an administrative and enforcement district. No season is written to it, and it must not be mistaken for a hunting unit.

And elk is the sharp case: "Elk Management Unit" (16) and "Elk Management Zone" are TWO DISTINCT GEOGRAPHIES — the zones are specific PLSS sections and townships inside the units ("Unit 1 — The following lands in Dawes and Sioux counties … T34N R57W: Sec. 21, 28, 36") — and one of them has no GIS layer at all.

licence.note:
AN EXPRESS GRANT OF BOTH USE AND REDISTRIBUTION: "There are no restrictions on the use and distribution of data provided in this map or service." Present on 9 of the 14 hunting items, and independently on the agency's own open-data portal description. No "may not redistribute" anywhere read.

THREE THINGS THAT MUST NOT BE CARRIED ACROSS. (1) FIVE of the fourteen items state NOTHING — Additional Antlerless Deer 2025, Dark Goose 2026 updates, Duck & Coot Updates 2026, Nebraska Game Refuge Boundary, and the Antelope open-data view — with accessInformation empty or null too, so even attribution is unstated for them, and they do not inherit the grant. (3) Service-level copyrightText is an empty string on all 14 FeatureServers and 13 of 14 layers — reading the service alone would have found no terms whatever in a state that grants them expressly.

ONE CLAUSE A REVIEWER SHOULD READ CLOSELY, reported rather than resolved: "suitability of this data for any use other than display". Grammatically it sits inside the warranty disclaimer — they warrant nothing beyond display — and it is not phrased as a prohibition on other uses, while the same sentence-pair opens by saying there are no restrictions on use and distribution. Overstating it into a prohibition would be as wrong as ignoring it.

geography.term: Antlerless Deer Zone (Zones 1–10); separately Wildlife Management Area and five further ODWC area types, Special Use Areas, and Wetland Development Units
geography.definedBy: ODWC's antlerless deer zones, which set antlerless allowances and antlerless days; buck and archery seasons are statewide
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount:
The deer layer is one of the few in the country where the counts legitimately agree: 10 units, 10 features, one polygon per zone, verified by enumerating distinct ZONENUMBER over a statewide envelope and finding exactly one feature for each of '1' to '10'.

The others fail in three different ways. Public_WMA_Boundaries returns 105 features for 104 distinct names, and "105 areas" is wrong TWICE OVER: fifteen of them are public FISHING areas (WMATYPE: WMA 83, PFA 15, PFHA 2, WMU 2, PHA 1, Other 2) and one unit is split across two polygons. ODWC's own layer description also says more areas exist that are not yet in the dataset, so the layer under-reports as well. Special Use Areas returns 107, of which only FOUR are AREATYPE "Hunting Area" — the rest are 53 Non-Ambulatory Area, 31 Safety Zone, 11 Waterfowl Refuge, 6 Walk-In turkey, 1 Trout Area and 1 blank, with one feature flagged CLOSED. Reading 107 as hunting areas would be the exact trap. Wetland Development Units return 160 features for 146 distinct names across 24 WMAs.

licence.statedAs: Permission to Use - Information presented on these pages is considered public information and may be distributed or copied. All photos and images are copyrighted and may not be reproduced without written permission of the Wildlife Department. Use of appropriate byline/photo/image credits is requested. The information contained in this web site is dynamic and will change over time. This information data and related graphics are not legal documents and are not intended to be used as such.
licence.attribution: Oklahoma Department of Wildlife Conservation
licence.note:
AN EXPRESS PERMISSION for information and data — "considered public information and may be distributed or copied" — with credit REQUESTED rather than required, and a narrow EXPRESS REFUSAL for photos and images absent written permission. The refusal is real and it bites exactly one thing: ODWC publishes its Antlerless Deer Zones map to the public as an IMAGE, so that graphic may not be reproduced. Under §8 that is not a blocker to answering — the underlying zone facts are encodable as structured data in North Ground's own words with the rule cited.

The two other instruments are NOT the terms and were kept separate. Service-level copyrightText is empty on all seven ODWC services. Two portal items carry a warranty disclaimer whose clause "No act of distribution shall be construed as or constitute any such warranty" PRESUPPOSES distribution and is not a refusal — and the other two items, including the deer-zones item itself, state NOTHING, so that disclaimer is not their terms either. Five candidate policy paths return the site's generic shell as soft 404s, so /disclaimer is the only ODWC data statement that exists.

geography.term: deer management unit
geography.definedBy: K.A.R. 115-4-6, titled "Deer; management units", authorized by K.S.A. 32-807, effective 30 April 1990 and last amended 29 July 2022. Subsections (a)–(s) name 19 units — 1 High Plains through 19 Kansas City urban — and the same regulation adds THREE named subunits, 4a Smoky Hill Air National Guard Range, 8a Fort Riley and 10a Fort Leavenworth urban, so the deer geography is 22 named regulatory areas.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: HERE THE ERROR RUNS BOTH WAYS, which is why both numbers matter. The primary layer returns 18 features with 18 distinct DMU values "UNIT 1" to "UNIT 18" — taken alone it UNDERSTATES the 19-unit system by one. Unit 19 lives in a separate service, DMU_19, whose only layer id is 2 and not 0. And the 18 are not 18 of 19 tiles: their AreaSQMile sums to 82,288 against Kansas's ~82,278 square miles, so THE 18 TILE THE WHOLE STATE and Unit 19 is an OVERLAY on top of them, not the nineteenth piece. A resolver that unioned all 19 would double-count the Kansas City area.
