The boundary information in the TIGER/Line Shapefiles are for statistical data collection and tabulation purposes only; their depiction and designation for statistical purposes does not constitute a determination of jurisdictional authority or rights of ownership or entitlement and they are not legal land descriptions.
theInheritedLicenceThatIsNotTheirs.finding: A FIFTH PLACE TERMS CAN MISLEAD, AND THE MOST DANGEROUS KIND, BECAUSE IT LOOKS PERMISSIVE. Both Kansas deer items, plus Sandhill Crane Zones, PC Zones and both Pronghorn items, carry this text in licenseInfo. Read on its own terms it GRANTS: "not copyrighted", "free to use in a product or publication" with acknowledgement. Reporting it would have given Kansas a permissive licence.
theInheritedLicenceThatIsNotTheirs.howItWasCaught: It is not KDWP's. The identical 775-character string appears on six unrelated items created up to six years apart, and the matching item DESCRIPTION is verbatim Census metadata listing 2010 SF1 population fields — POP2010, WHITE, BLACK, MED_AGE, RENTER_OCC — that exist in none of these layers. It is inherited boilerplate carried by the authoring template, describing TIGER/Line rather than Kansas hunting geography.
theInheritedLicenceThatIsNotTheirs.andItIsEvidenceAgainstFitness: The same text says the boundaries "are not legal land descriptions", while K.A.R. 115-4-6 defines the units by highway metes and bounds. So even taken at face value it would be arguing that the polygons are not the legal boundary — which is a second reason not to treat it as a grant.
theInheritedLicenceThatIsNotTheirs.theNarrowProhibitionThatIsKdwps: From the agency's own Notices page, under the heading "Copyright", complete: "Any use of the photos, graphics and logos on this site without permission from the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks is prohibited." Scoped to photos, graphics and logos; it says nothing about data, geometry, regulation text or season facts.

geography.term: COUNTY — Georgia has no wildlife-management-unit system
geography.definedBy: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. Subject 391-4-2, which defines every season by enumerated county lists rather than by units
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 159 counties, matching Georgia exactly. Deer has NO named zones — rule 391-4-2-.27 groups counties into six season groups, carried in the GIS only as the printed map's legend colours (GREEN 133, MAGENTA 9, ORANGE 9, GRAY 4, CYAN 2, YELLOW 2 = 159). Bear has three named zones over 51 counties, and the other 108 carry an EMPTY STRING, which is not a zone. WMAs cannot be counted from the layer at all: 107 distinct names ending "WMA", inside 126 game-managed names, inside 169 distinct names, inside 222 features.
geography.administrativeFieldsThatMustNeverBeServe: The layer carries DMU (1–9) and WRD_Region (1–6) fields, and "Deer Management Unit" appears ZERO TIMES in the 241,617 characters of Subject 391-4-2. They are administrative and biological, not regulatory geography. A resolver that answered from DMU would be inventing a hunting unit Georgia does not have.
geography.parityCertifiedBySetComparisonNotByCount: Alligator zones 1–9 match rule 391-4-2-.21(3) county-for-county (13/6/14/10/17/9/7/7/13), and Bear Southern and Bear Central match .22(4) and .22(5) exactly. Comparing SETS rather than counts is what made the Bartow conflict visible at all.

lawVersusGis.finding: THE BARTOW COUNTY CONFLICT, AND IT IS INVISIBLE AT THE COUNT LEVEL. Georgia's codified rule and Georgia's own map layer disagree about whether Bartow County has an either-sex deer season — while both sets contain 133 counties, so every count check passes. Only a set comparison finds it.
lawVersusGis.lawSays: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 391-4-2-.27, by enumerated county list.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: The GA_County_zones layer's either-sex attribute for Bartow.
lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: Neither side was declared stale, because the evidence does not settle which is right — and that is the honest state. What was established is that the disagreement is real and that 133 = 133 conceals it.
lawVersusGis.doNotServe: Bartow must be UNKNOWN for deer, and the rest of the either-sex set must not be published as though the layer and the rule agreed. §8 in the other direction too: do not discard the other 158 counties over one.
lawVersusGis.servablePathFromTheLaw: The rule's own county list, which is enumerated in parseable text — the same county-join path Kentucky and North Carolina use.

threeFinerThanCountyRulesWithNoGeometry.finding: Georgia's only regulatory geometry is the county, and three deer rules are FINER than a county: Forsyth south of GA Hwy 20, Fulton north of GA Hwy 92, and Glynn within Jekyll Island. A point-in-county resolver returns a confidently WRONG answer inside all three.
threeFinerThanCountyRulesWithNoGeometry.andAlligatorIsWorse: Rule 391-4-2-.21(3) says "the State is divided into eleven hunting zones" and lists 1, 1A, 2–8, 8A, 9. The GIS carries only the nine numeric ones. Zone 1A is Lake Walter F. George — a 96-inch minimum length against the statewide 48 — and 8A is Fort Stewart, and BOTH LIE INSIDE COUNTIES ASSIGNED TO OTHER ZONES, so the county layer returns the wrong zone for a hunter on that lake or that base. Alligator is servable for zones 1–9 only if 1A and 8A are explicitly carved out as unresolved.

findings.note: THE STATUTORY BASIS FOR GEORGIA'S HOURS IS UNREACHABLE, and the failure is the state's own access route. The general 30-minute rule is in the guide but nowhere in the Georgia Administrative Code, verified with a positive control. Its basis must be O.C.G.A. Title 27, and the General Assembly links the Code to a LexisNexis path that redirects to a sign-in error page, while legis.ga.gov/laws/code client-side 404s and the Secretary of State's statute links run through an Angular app the browser refused to open. So the hours rule can be served citing the guide, and NOT yet with a statutory cite. Do not fabricate one.

geography.term: COUNTY — ODNR's own field is "County_Bag_Limit" with classes "Two Deer County", "Three Deer County", "Four Deer County"; layered with waterfowl Zones A/B/C, spring turkey South and Northeast Zones, river otter Zones A/B, and a Disease Surveillance Area
geography.definedBy: OAC Chapter 1501:31 — which could not be read; see the access blocker below
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: THREE separate instances in one state, all running toward looking like more coverage. (1) The deer layers return 107 features for Ohio's 88 counties: 19 of the distinct COUNTY values are TOWNSHIP STRINGS — "Allen County, Auglaize Township" and the like, Allen 6, Crawford 4, Delaware 3, Hancock 3, Union 2, Morrow 1 — each carrying attributes IDENTICAL to its parent county row, so they are redundant duplicates. Six of them are also STALE: the 2026-27 change list says the disease surveillance area expanded to include all of Allen County, and the DSA layer correctly now says "All townships", so Allen's six township polygons are pre-expansion leftovers. The 88 decompose as 71 three-deer, 8 two-deer in two textually distinct variants, 5 four-deer and 4 DSA, summing to 88. (2) The quail layer returns 89: the 89th is OBJECTID 91 with COUNTY = "Tri-Valley" — a WILDLIFE AREA smuggled into a county field. (3) DOW Districts returns 6 for 5 districts, and the sixth is "Central Office" at 2045 Morse Road with Shape__Area 1,521,780 against 174–265 BILLION for the real districts — A BUILDING FOOTPRINT, caught by comparing areas rather than trusting the count.
geography.theUnitIdentifierIsNotAStableKey: No layer carries a FIPS code or any numeric identifier. The join field is the free-text COUNTY name, and it is not clean, for the three reasons above. Layers 6 and 7 appear to be the same table published twice. Normalising the county set to 88 and classifying the non-county rows is engineering work, not a data gap — but it must happen before any of this becomes a resolver.

conflict.finding: THE DSA DEER BAG LIMIT IS SIX VERSUS THREE. Two current ODNR publications disagree on how many deer a hunter may take in the Disease Surveillance Area: the digest says six, the live GIS service says three. Four whole counties — Allen, Hardin, Marion, Wyandot — and thirteen named townships across Crawford, Delaware, Hancock, Morrow and Union are affected.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: A bag limit is exactly the kind of number that must render as CONFLICT rather than resolve to one side. And §8 cuts the other way too: the other 84 counties are unaffected and their bag classes agree with the digest legend, so this blocks the DSA and not Ohio deer generally — do not throw away the 84 to avoid the 4.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: OAC Chapter 1501:31, which is behind the access blocker above.

findings.note: SPRING TURKEY SERVES AN EXPIRED SEASON. ODNR says the 2027 spring dates and hours are "To be announced", available by January 2027, while layer 4 serves the spring 2026 window as current attributes. Spring turkey must be UNKNOWN for any 2027 date and the layer's season fields must not be read — though the zone geometry and the two zone names are usable now.

geography.term: Deer Management Zone (Zones 1–4)
geography.definedBy: 250-RICR-60-00-9 § 9.7(B), which enumerates the towns in each zone: Zone 1 twenty-six towns, Zone 2 twelve, Zone 3 Patience and Prudence Islands, Zone 4 New Shoreham (Block Island).
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 4 units against 47 FEATURES, and both were enumerated rather than either inferred. Distinct DeerMU = 4, matching the regulation exactly. Distinct TWNCODE = 39, every Rhode Island municipality. Distinct (DeerMU, TWNCODE) pairs = 40, and the one extra pair is Portsmouth, which appears under BOTH zone 2 and zone 3 — exactly as § 9.7(B) requires, because Prudence and Patience Islands are part of Portsmouth. Features per zone: 26 + 12 + 8 + 1 = 47, the eight being the two islands as polygon parts. So the layer is municipality-and-island-part polygons attributed to a zone, not a four-polygon dissolve; a dissolve on DeerMU yields the four legal units, and 26 + 12 + 1 = 39 municipalities closes the arithmetic against the regulation.
geography.deerIsTheOnlyZonedSpecies: Established by scanning every occurrence of "zone" in the full regulation: all 20 are deer (§§ 9.7, 9.7.6, 9.7.7, 9.8) plus one unrelated use ("buffer zones" at a management area). Everything else is regulated statewide with named-area exceptions.

findings.note: RIDEM'S NAMED-AREA GEOGRAPHY IS PARTLY BROKEN AT THE SOURCE, which is a finding about the publisher rather than about us: the agency's own "RIDEM Hunting Area Index" web map points at two layers that no longer exist, and the Hunting_Atlas service self-describes as the 2013/2014 season. What remains, layer 20, is only 12 of 61 features on RIDEM land — the rest being a water utility, municipalities, The Nature Conservancy and federal refuges — so serving it as "state hunting areas" would be a false claim. It must be modelled by its Type field or not drawn.

geography.term: Wildlife Management Unit, with "subunit" for the subdivided ones
geography.definedBy: 10 App. V.S.A. § 2b, "Wildlife Management Units"
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: They agree, checked rather than assumed: 21 features and 21 distinct BOUNDARY values — A, B, C, D1, D2, E1, E2, F1, F2, G, H, I, J1, J2, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q. The subdivided units are separate regulatory units, not cartographic splits, which is the same shape as Connecticut's 4A/4B.
geography.threeGeographiesNotOne: A Vermont coordinate does not resolve to a single unit: WMUs, waterfowl hunting zones and state game refuges are three distinct hunting geographies.

licence.statedAs: CC BY-SA
licence.attribution: VT ANR
licence.note:
THE ENTIRE LICENCE IS TWO WORDS, and they are a grant: "CC BY-SA". No conditions paragraph, no prose, no prohibition. CC BY-SA affirmatively permits redistribution including commercially; its requirements are attribution and ShareAlike. SHARESHALIKE IS A REAL AND CONSEQUENTIAL CONDITION — an adaptation of the geometry must itself be licensed CC BY-SA — but it is a condition on the form of onward licensing, not a refusal, and it is not triggered by using the data to answer a question.

THE VERSION IS INFERRED, NOT WRITTEN. The Agency wrote only "CC BY-SA" with no version. ArcGIS Hub's structured field resolves it to Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International, so 4.0 comes from a machine field rather than from anything the Agency stated. Recorded as inferred.

AND THE SERVICE SAYS LESS THAN NOTHING: layer 164's copyrightText is an empty string while the parent service root says "VTANR GIS" — an attribution, not a licence. Reading either would have concluded no terms.

termsDifferPerDatasetInOneService.finding: THE SHARPEST CASE OF THIS FOUND ANYWHERE. Same host, same service, same account, same publication window, DIFFERENT LICENCE STATE per dataset. Waterfowl Hunting Zones VT: layer copyrightText empty, portal item licenseInfo null, accessInformation null, structuredLicense type "none". State Game Refuges and Controlled Hunting Areas: the same. The WMU layer's CC BY-SA does NOT extend to either of them.
termsDifferPerDatasetInOneService.andEvenWithinOneDatasetFamily: ANR Lands (Parcel) carries CC BY-SA plus an express condition — "Secondary distribution must be accompanied by this documentation. Credit should always be given to the data source when this data is transferred or printed" — which presupposes secondary distribution is permitted and is not a prohibition. A sibling item titled "ANR Land Dataset (Parcel)" carries licenseInfo "". So the instruments disagree inside one dataset family.
termsDifferPerDatasetInOneService.consequence: Vermont cannot be classified once. It must be recorded per layer, as Indiana and Nebraska must.

theTermsPageThatReturns200AndDoesNotExis.finding: geodata.vermont.gov/pages/terms-of-use returns HTTP 200 AND THERE IS NO SUCH PAGE. The 200 is the ArcGIS Hub client shell, which answers 200 for any unknown slug. This is the output that would otherwise be reported as a terms page.
theTermsPageThatReturns200AndDoesNotExis.provenTwoWays: (1) The site item's own page registry lists 12 pages and terms-of-use is not among them. (2) POSITIVE CONTROL BY BYTE COUNT: a page that IS in the registry, /pages/changelog, returned 65,865 bytes against the nonexistent page's 65,868 — the identical shell.
theTermsPageThatReturns200AndDoesNotExis.andOnePageIsGenuinelyUnread: anr.vermont.gov/maps/gis-data returned HTTP 403 to this reader while anr.vermont.gov/maps returned 200 on the same host by the same method, so the 403 is page-specific. Its contents are UNKNOWN and may contain terms. Three further guessed URLs returned 404 and are recorded so they are never reported as sources.

geography.term: COUNTY — TPWD's own regulation index is literally "Seasons by County"
geography.definedBy: TPWD's per-county regulation pages, one per county, at /regulations/outdoor-annual/regs/counties/<slug>
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: Here they agree and it is the one Texas layer where they do: the selector on TPWD's county index contains exactly 254 options, Texas has 254 counties, and TPWD's county layer returns 254 features with 254 distinct CNTY_NM. Species zones compose ON TOP of the county and none is an independent published unit system: deer North/South is assigned PER COUNTY on the county page, dove is 3 zones = 3 features, duck is 3 units = 3 features defined by highway lines, goose is 2 = 2.
geography.theCountyGeometryBELONGSToAnotherAgency: TX_Counties_Labeled's licenseInfo is NOT TPWD's and must never be reported as such — it is the Texas Department of Transportation's: "Copyright 2014. Texas Department of Transportation. This data was produced for internal use within the Texas Department of Transportation and made available to the public for informational purposes only... It is intended for internal use only." Counties are Texas's regulatory unit, so the geometry North Ground would need has a different publisher with stricter terms than the wildlife agency's, and TPWD's terms do not reach it.

licence.statedAs: © Copyright Texas Parks and Wildlife Department. No part of this work may be copied, reproduced, or translated in any form or medium without the prior written consent of Texas Parks Wildlife Department except where specifically noted. No portion of this work may be sold, either by itself or as part of larger work, without the express written permission of the TPWD. Commercial Use: To obtain permission to reproduce the information (text or graphics) contained on the TPWD Web site for any commercial purpose, submit the specifics of your request in writing to Communications Division — Web Services Team Leader, Texas Parks & Wildlife Department.
licence.attribution: Texas Parks and Wildlife Department
licence.note:
THE AGENCY'S OWN COPYRIGHT POLICY IS A RESTRICTION, not a condition, and it is the governing instrument. Prior written consent is the default; selling any portion requires express written permission; commercial reproduction requires a written request. North Ground is a commercial product, so that reaches us directly.

"EXCEPT WHERE SPECIFICALLY NOTED" IS THE OPERATIVE CLAUSE, and exactly one dataset is noted: MuleDeer_ManagementUnites_2019 adds "These data are in the public domain" — the ONLY Texas hunting dataset with an affirmative reuse permission. One other adds "This data is not intended to be used for profit", which is a statement of intent rather than an express prohibition; it is reported as the words and not converted.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT PREVENT, because overstating it would be as wrong as ignoring it. It prevents reproducing TPWD's prose and zone-map graphics verbatim and prevents selling its work, so it prevents storing and redistributing TPWD geometry inside a commercial product without consent. It does NOT prevent reading the rules and encoding the legal facts as structured data in North Ground's own words with the source cited (§8), and it does not prevent live reads of TPWD's public endpoints under the standing US live-service-only decision.

The service level would have misled in the other direction: copyrightText is an empty string on six services and a bare attribution on the rest, so stopping there would have reported Texas as stating no terms.

geography.term: LOCALITY — a county or an independent city. Virginia has no WMU, GMU or zone system
geography.definedBy: 4VAC15-90-10, which opens "It shall be lawful to hunt deer in the following localities, including the cities and towns therein, during the following seasons" and then enumerates locality by locality; 4VAC15-240 does the same for turkey, its sections titled "Open season; certain counties and areas".
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 133 localities, classified from the layer's own NAMELSAD field as 95 "… County" plus 38 "… City", and independently corroborated by 133 distinct STCOFIPS values. Virginia's independent cities are units in their own right, so a 95-county model would silently drop 38 of them.
geography.theOneNamedZoneIsComposable: 4VAC15-20-10 B: "‘Elk Management Zone’ means the Counties of (i) Buchanan, (ii) Dickenson, and (iii) Wise, and the cities and towns therein." All three resolve in the DWR layer as single-part features (FIPS 51027, 51051, 51195), so the zone is composable from county polygons without inventing geography — the same shape as Delaware's CWD zone.

licence.statedAs: By accepting data provided by the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources (DWR), you must agree to the following conditions of release and acknowledge the following disclaimers issued by DWR: A. Conditions of Release — Data are available by permission of the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources. Use of data in publications, either digital or hardcopy, must be cited as follows: <dataset name>. <date acquired>. Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources.
licence.attribution: Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources
licence.note:
NOT A REFUSAL, AND NOT A GRANT, AND THE AMBIGUITY IS IN ONE SENTENCE. The citation requirement is a CONDITION, and it is phrased for "publications, either digital or hardcopy", which presupposes downstream publication is contemplated. The liability and accuracy paragraphs are disclaimers. There is no express "may not redistribute" in any of the three instruments, and one was looked for.

THE UNRESOLVED CLAUSE: "Data are available by permission of the Virginia Department of Wildlife Resources." That supports two readings — these data are released BY DWR's permission subject to the citation condition, or you must OBTAIN DWR's permission — and nothing on the page disambiguates it. It is not resolved here and it is not reported as a prohibition. One fact bears on it without settling it: the live REST services are served publicly with no gate, every endpoint returning 200 unauthenticated, while the click-through "I Agree" sits on the separate data-download path.

VIRGINIA IS THE STATE WHERE THE PORTAL ITEM DOES NOT RESCUE THE SERVICE. Six DWR items were read individually and licenseInfo is null or empty in every case; the DWR Hub site's own config carries licenseInfo null and its footer "Terms of Use" link is an unfilled placeholder, href="#".

theCountyGeometryBelongsToAnotherAgency.finding: The locality polygons are VGIN's data redistributed by DWR — DWR's own layer copyrightText says so: "Virginia Geographic Information Network (VGIN), and the Census and Localities and Towns submitting data to the project". VGIN's own terms, read separately: the boundaries "are intended for cartographic use and spatial analysis only, and not for use as legal descriptions or property surveys", plus a warranty disclaimer. No attribution condition and no redistribution restriction — a use-limitation caveat, not a refusal.
theCountyGeometryBelongsToAnotherAgency.whyItIsRecordedSeparately: Two publishers, two instruments, and the geometry North Ground would need is the second one's. Borrowing DWR's terms onto VGIN's data, or the reverse, would misname the authority.

geography.term: COUNTY
geography.definedBy: West Virginia Code Chapter 20, with seasons and open counties published annually by WVDNR in the regulations summary — which itself states "This pamphlet is a summary… It is for informational purposes only and subject to change… the West Virginia Code and the West Virginia Code of State Rules are, at all times, the controlling laws". No Code of State Rules text was established: the CSR index loads but is a postback form, and a guessed DocId returns HTTP 200 carrying a scanned image-only PDF, so that endpoint cannot confirm a document's identity and no CSR document is cited.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 55 features and 55 distinct Name values, matching West Virginia's 55 counties.
geography.countyIsNotTheWholeGeography:
Sub-county splits exist and DIFFER PER SPECIES. Deer has four published split counties with division-line descriptions — Fayette, Greenbrier, Kanawha and Mineral. Bear has six counties with inline qualifiers: Barbour "West of Route 92 and Route 250…", Braxton "West of I-79", Clay "North of Elk River", Mineral "East of New Creek", Monroe "West of Route 219", Upshur "West of Route 20".

AND MINERAL COUNTY IS THE TRAP: its BEAR qualifier ("East of New Creek") is described differently from its DEER division line (U.S. 220S to SR 972, SR 972S to U.S. 50, U.S. 50W to SR 93, SR 93S to the Grant County line). It was NOT established that these are the same line, so one split-county geometry must not be assumed to serve both species.

The CWD Containment Area is a second county-composed geography, and it has TWO DIFFERENT COUNTY SETS in one named area: eight counties for the baiting and feeding restriction, and only seven for the carcass-transport restriction, with Pendleton excluded from the latter.

licence.statedAs: This dataset provides information on wildlife management areas for general reference and planning purposes. These boundaries are not survey-grade and should not be regarded as exact property boundaries. Users should always ensure they have the most up-to-date data. While efforts have been made to ensure accuracy, completeness, and reliability, users should exercise caution and independent judgment when interpreting and utilizing the data. Crediting the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources when using this dataset in projects or analyses is appreciated. WVDNR does not guarantee the accuracy, completeness, or currency of the data. WVDNR is not liable for any damages or losses resulting from the use or misuse of this dataset. By using this dataset, you acknowlege and accept these terms.
licence.attribution: West Virginia Division of Natural Resources, Wildlife Resources Section, GIS Unit
licence.note:
NOT A REFUSAL. Every instrument is a warranty disclaimer, an accuracy or currency caveat, a fitness-for-legal-use limitation, or an attribution REQUEST — "Crediting the West Virginia Division of Natural Resources… is appreciated". Appreciated, not required, and that distinction is worth keeping: it is weaker than Florida's "Please acknowledge" and weaker still than a condition. No prohibition on redistribution, commercial use or derived products appears anywhere read.

THE DOCUMENTED VIEWS HAVE TERMS AND THE UNDOCUMENTED SERVICES HAVE NONE, and they must not be borrowed across: WildlifeManagementAreas, CWD_Containment_Area, WV_Counties and WV_Public_Lands each return licenseInfo as an empty string, while the curated view items carry the text above. And one sibling copy is not a licence at all — the DOT-hosted WMA copy's service-level copyrightText reads "Questions or comments should be directed to Alicia R. Mein, Alicia.R.Mein@wv.gov of the WVDNR."

The CWD item carries something useful in its own right: "If there are discrepancies between this layer and the WVDNR Hunting Regulations, the official regulations take precedence" — the publisher stating the precedence rule itself, as Maine and Washington do.

geography.term: GAME ZONE (Game Zones 1–4)
geography.definedBy: S.C. Code § 50-1-60, "Division of State into game zones": "For the purpose of protection and management of wildlife, the State is divided into four zones". Its own history establishes currency: 2014 Act No. 227, SECTION 1, eff. 1 July 2015, whose Effect-of-Amendment note records that it "substituted 'four zones' for 'six zones'; and deleted former paragraphs (5) and (6)" — so the four-zone system is the one in force and the six-zone system is superseded.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 4 = 4, checked rather than assumed, and unusually clean: a groupBy returns exactly four groups of one, with a coded-value domain named SCDNR_GameZone. No status field, no closures, no safety zones, no NOT MANAGED rows, no boundary segments — GameZone='1' returns ONE closed ring of 784 vertices. Per-zone extents are geographically correct. The statute's own composition closes the arithmetic: 15 + 15 + 13 whole counties = 43, plus the three split counties Oconee, Pickens and Greenville = 46 = South Carolina's county total.
geography.theOutstandingParityCheck: THE GAME ZONE 1/2 LINE IS NOT A COUNTY LINE — the statute describes it as the main line of the Norfolk Southern Railroad and S.C. Highway 183. The drawn geometry was NOT verified against that description, and that parity check is outstanding. Recording it as outstanding rather than as done is the point: every other check on this layer passed, which is exactly the situation in which an unrun check gets forgotten.
geography.fourUnitSystemsAndOnlyOneCarriesTheSeaso: R.123-40 organises WMA rules as Game Zone → a generic "Other WMAs" class, a generic US Forest Service class, and named exception areas — 74 entries across the four zones, of which 4 are the generic Other class and 2 the generic USFS class, so it is NOT a list of WMA properties. Category I and Category II Designated Waterfowl Areas and Public Dove Fields are third and fourth systems, the dove fields being "all areas as published by the Department in the annual Laws and Regulations Guide". Only the Game Zone is the unit the seasons are written in.

licenceAbsent.finding: No grant and no prohibition. The portal item's licenseInfo is a warranty disclaimer plus an indemnity plus an accuracy caveat, with no attribution requirement, no describe-your-changes condition and no express "may not redistribute". And the strongest permission language SCDNR actually publishes is an AVAILABILITY statement, not a licence: "GIS data produced and maintained by SCDNR is available free of charge to the public in an effort to facilitate natural resource decision-making, analysis and education in South Carolina." Inflating that into an affirmative redistribution licence would be as wrong as collapsing the disclaimer into a prohibition.
whereLooked: service and layer copyrightText on South_Carolina_Game_Zones — the empty string at both levels
the Public Lands service — also empty
portal item licenseInfo on the Game Zones item, the Public Lands Viewer item and the Public Lands hub-site item
the SCDNR Open Data group description, which PRESCRIBES that disclaimer org-wide
https://www.dnr.sc.gov/gis.html — the agency's own GIS page
licenceAbsent.controlForTheAbsence: Two controls. The identical disclaimer text appears on three separate items AND is prescribed org-wide by the SCDNR Open Data group description, which instructs publishers to "Include the disclaimer below in the Terms of Use section" — so it is a house disclaimer rather than a dataset term, and it is still reported per instrument rather than borrowed across datasets. Separately, two guessed policy URLs returned 404 against a positive control on the same host by the same method (dnr.sc.gov/maps.html, HTTP 200, 39,740 bytes).
licenceAbsent.whyItsOwnStateAndNotReachability: Every endpoint answered 200. One practical limit is technical rather than legal, and worth recording: the Game Zones service exposes capabilities "Query" only, with no Extract, while the Public Lands service exposes "Query,Extract".
licenceAbsent.theGuideCarriesNoNotice: The 130-page annual regulations guide contained zero hits for "copyright", "©", "All rights reserved" and any reproduction-permission string across its extracted text. Reported as OBSERVED, not as an absence of copyright in law: a notice may exist inside page artwork the extractor did not reach.

geography.term: Deer Management Unit (Units 1–6), plus Turkey Management Units, Bear Hunt Zones and Elk Hunt Zones — four species-specific systems
geography.definedBy: TFWC Proclamation 26-11 §I.A: "For the purposes of these hunting regulations, the State of Tennessee is hereby divided into six (6) deer management units"; §IV.B does the same for five turkey units and §II.A for six bear hunt zones.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 6 units against 95 FEATURES — one polygon per Tennessee county. PARITY IS CERTIFIED, not assumed: all six county lists were parsed from Proclamation 26-11 and compared to the layer's DMU field — 21/19/18/14/9/14 = 95, every county's unit assignment identical, zero differences in either direction. Turkey likewise: five units, five features, and the parsed lists form an exact partition of all 95 counties (7/12/35/24/17) with no county missing or duplicated.
geography.bearHasNoGeometryAndItsDefinitionsAreSub: Six bear hunt zones are designated and NO boundary layer exists, and the definitions are finer than a county: "Cocke (North of I-40)", "Jefferson (East of Hwy 411)", "Anderson (West of I-75 and North of Old Lake City Hwy and North of Dutch Valley Road)", "Overton (East of Hwy 111)". A county resolver would answer confidently and wrongly inside every one.

licenceAbsent.finding: No licence on any layer North Ground would serve, and no prohibition either. The deer-unit dataset is silent at all four instruments: service copyrightText empty, layer copyrightText empty, portal item licenseInfo ABSENT, and the ArcGIS Hub dataset record reporting license "none" with structuredLicense type "none". Other layers carry warranty and liability disclaimers, which are not refusals, or bare attributions — including one that is a staff member's personal name.
whereLooked: DeerMgmtUnitCounties service copyrightText, layer-0 copyrightText, portal item licenseInfo and the Hub dataset record
HuntingAllowed, QuotaHuntsOnly and SafetyZoneAreas — service, layer and item
Hunting_Allowed — where the service field is empty and the LAYER field is populated
licenceAbsent.controlForTheAbsence: A url-scoped item search for BearReserves returned HTTP 200 with total=0, i.e. no portal item exists and there is no item-level instrument to read — and the control is that the identical search shape returned total=1 for TurkeyMgmtUnits, ElkHuntZones_2024 and DeerMgmtUnitCounties. So the zero is a true zero.
licenceAbsent.whatWouldUnblockIt: TWRA stating terms for its datasets, or confirming that the Hub site's CC-BY-SA reaches them.
licenceAbsent.whyItsOwnStateAndNotReachability: Every service answered 200 and parity was certified against the proclamation.

theHubSiteLicenceIsNotTheDatasetsLicence.finding: The portal item for the "Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency Data HUB" carries licenseInfo "CC-BY-SA" — and that is the licence field of the HUB SITE APPLICATION ITEM, not of any dataset. Attributing it to the deer-unit layer would be reporting one item's terms as another's, which is the same error as Kansas's Census boilerplate in the opposite direction: there the inherited text was too permissive, here the permissive text is real but attached to the wrong object.
theHubSiteLicenceIsNotTheDatasetsLicence.whatItIsEvidenceOf: An intent to license the Hub's contents openly, and it is the only positive licence string found for Tennessee. Whether it reaches a given dataset is UNRESOLVED.
theHubSiteLicenceIsNotTheDatasetsLicence.andOneLicenceFieldIsACurrencyWarning: ElkHuntZones_2024's licenseInfo is not a licence at all: "To be reviewed each year after season-setting commission meeting is held; may be altered prior to commission meeting to reflect changes being requested of the commission by TWRA staff." That says the layer may depict changes only REQUESTED of the Commission and not yet adopted — so it is a blocker for serving elk zones AS LAW, and a blocker for nothing else. It is the same shape as Michigan's rescinded units: the publisher telling you its own layer is not the instrument.

silenceIsNotRefusal: Two different states of the world are both recorded as blocked, and they are undone differently. SILENCE (UNRESOLVED) means no grant is stated either way: the publisher may simply never have been asked, so a person must ask it. A REFUSAL (RESTRICTED, or redistribution PROHIBITED) means the publisher has answered, and the answer is no: reading its terms more carefully will not change them, and only a written exception from it would. Reporting the two identically would make a refusal look like an errand.
reachabilityIsNotLicence: A source that cannot be reached SECURELY is blocked for a different reason than one whose terms refuse us, and the two must not be merged. Arizona is the first: its own GIS host has served an expired certificate since 2022, so North Ground has never been able to read its terms at all. Recording that as a licence finding would assert something about terms nobody has read; recording it as 'no source' would be false, because the authority publishes one. It is its own state, and the remedy belongs to the authority rather than to us.
aWarrantyDisclaimerIsNotALicence: Several states answer a licence question with a WARRANTY disclaimer, which is a different legal instrument: it disclaims liability for accuracy and says nothing about reuse. Nevada's whole statement is one. Reading "no warranty" as "no permission" would invent a refusal; reading it as permission would invent a grant. Both are UNRESOLVED, and the note says which kind of silence it is, because a disclaimer means the publisher HAS written terms and they simply do not address use — which is a different ask than a publisher who has written nothing.
threeWaysAFindingCanLackALicence: A finding carries exactly one of: `licence` (terms were read, whatever they say), `reachability` (the service could not be reached securely, so its terms could not be read either — Arizona), or `licenceAbsent` (the service is fine and the publisher has stated nothing — Utah). They are not interchangeable because the next action differs: read the terms, ask the authority to fix its certificate, or ask the authority to state terms at all.

openDecisionForTheOwner.question: Does an ABSENCE of stated terms block a LIVE READ of an authority's own public service, or only a stored copy?
openDecisionForTheOwner.whyItIsBeingAsked: It is the single highest-leverage classification decision left in the United States, and it is not mine to make. The standing owner decision is that US GIS is live-service only — no US state polygons stored, certify live — and Idaho is already SERVED that way with redistribution UNRESOLVED and storedCopyPermitted false. If an unstated licence blocks only a stored copy, then every state below in `statesWhereNothingRefusesUs` is currently reported as blocked while nothing refuses us, which is exactly the over-strict error §8 names — and §8 also says a refusal always looks defensible, which is why an unnecessary one is never reported by anyone.
openDecisionForTheOwner.whatIsNotBeingClaimed: Nothing has been reclassified on this argument. Every state below is still reported LICENCE_BLOCKED, which is the conservative reading. §62 puts source integrity above user usefulness and §46 asks for human review of high-impact changes, so the argument is recorded and the decision is left open rather than taken.

theRiskInEachDirection.ifTermsAreReclassifiedAndThatIsWrong: North Ground would serve geometry it had no permission to serve. A licensing exposure, outward-facing, and the owner's to accept or refuse.
theRiskInEachDirection.ifTheyAreNotAndThatIsWrong: North Ground reports itself unable to answer in states where nothing refuses it, and the states stay unbuilt. No hunter is harmed today, and the cost is invisible — which is precisely why it needs stating.

liveReadDisposition.decision: Owner: unstated redistribution rights block copying and republishing, not ordinary read-only use of a public live authority service. See CLAUDE.md §44, 'Reading a live service is not copying it'.
howEachWasVerified: the service was called anonymously over ordinary HTTPS — no authentication, no referrer, no spoofed user agent
its layer metadata and Query capability were read
one feature was read to see whether the service returns an identifier that can map to a canonical zone id
robots.txt was fetched for each self-hosted host
latency was measured, because a production path needs a service that answers quickly enough to serve
liveReadDisposition.whatThisDoesNotGrant: No stored copy, mirror, redistribution or bulk extraction. `licencePermitsStoredCopy` refuses LIVE_READ_NO_STATED_TERMS structurally rather than by reading the redistribution field.

MA.evidence: HTTP 200 anonymous, 281 ms, Query supported, 15 features. Identifier field DMZ carries 1-14 with zone 4 split 4N/4S — a clean single zone system, which is why Massachusetts is the one of the eight that could be served today. The ArcGIS Online item is ORGANISATION-owned. Certified 2026-10-06: 87 points, 0 disagreements, 0 in two units, authority p90 103 ms, production p90 235 ms.

UT.supersedes: The earlier entry said only that Utah publishes one combined set of 686 boundaries and that which items are huntable geography is a modelling decision. That was right and vague; this is the measurement.
UT.structure: 687 features: 654 Active, 19 Inactive, 10 Pending, 4 with no status. 151 carry BTYPE='CWMU' (Cooperative Wildlife Management Units, which are private-land cooperative units); the other 536 have BTYPE null or blank. BoundaryID IS a clean key — unique across all 654 Active rows — so the obstacle is not identity.
UT.theObstacle: A UTAH POINT DOES NOT RESOLVE TO ONE UNIT. Vernal falls inside 25 Active boundaries and Moab inside 13. Utah publishes one combined set in which different species and hunt types carve the same ground differently — the names show it directly: 'Nebo (excludes West Face)' and 'Nebo-West Face' are separate rows over adjacent ground. A zone layer whose resolver returns 25 answers for one coordinate is not a zone layer, and North Ground's resolver deliberately refuses to pick one of several.
UT.whatItWouldTake: Not a licence, not an endpoint, and not a key: a model of which boundary applies to which species and hunt type, which Utah encodes in the hunt tables beside this layer rather than in the geometry. That is the same shape as Louisiana's seven species geographies, except Utah's overlap WITHIN one layer rather than across layers, so `speciesScope` alone does not answer it.
UT.aNoteOnHowThisWasMeasured: The first attempt returned ZERO boundaries at all four points and would have been recorded as 'Utah's layer does not cover its own towns'. The `where=Status='Active'` clause was malformed — the same query without it returned 25 and 13, and a count query using it returned HTTP 400. The checker was broken, not the data, and a zero that agrees with no expectation is exactly when to doubt the checker first.

MS.evidence: The authority does NOT refuse us. Layer 7 is "MDWFP DEER ZONES", polygon, copyrightText "", and curl retrieves it normally. Node's fetch fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE because the server sends ONLY the leaf certificate: `openssl s_client` shows a chain of depth 0 with issuer "GlobalSign Atlas R3 OV TLS CA 2026 Q1" never presented. Positive controls on the same run: Utah and the Esri-hosted services both returned 200.
MS.whyNotServedYet: An incomplete TLS chain on the authority's server, which is OUR side to handle by supplying the missing intermediate — never by disabling verification.

CT.evidence: The layer serves (HTTP 200, 13 zones, Query supported) and the registry's stored service URL was elided to '...' and had to be recovered through ArcGIS Online search. The item is owned by `karenz` with NO orgId — a PERSONAL account — while its accessInformation claims "Connecticut Department of Energy and Environmental Protection". A searchable CT-government-owned equivalent was not found.
CT.whyNotServedYet: An item on a personal account asserting an authority's attribution is not that authority's own published service, and §41A requires every line to trace to one. This is the 'a permissive licence can belong to another publisher entirely' hazard, so Connecticut is held on PROVENANCE rather than on licence.
CT.scopeLimitThatMustNotBeFlattened: The dataset is scoped to PRIVATE LAND deer and turkey reporting zones by town; on state land hunting is governed by DEEP's hunting-area and lottery system, so a zone answer on state land answers the wrong question.

AL.supersedes: The earlier entry read LIVE_READ_CLEAR_WRONG_LAYER_RECORDED, on the assumption that the right layer existed and the registry named the wrong one. It does not exist.
AL.evidence: ADCNR's own ArcGIS server was enumerated: 47 services at the root and nine in SWAP, and NONE is a deer or turkey season zone. The service the registry recorded, WildlifeManagementAreas/MapServer, has exactly ONE layer — 'Wildlife Management Area', which is properties. The Feature_Services folder is empty. ArcGIS Online returns ZERO items for 'Alabama deer season zone', 'Alabama turkey season zone' and title:"Deer Season Zones" Alabama.
AL.positiveControl: The same search method returns 176 items for 'deer season zone' — including California's BIOS_Admin Deer Hunt Zones and Indiana's Deer Reduction Zones — and 61 for 'Alabama hunting'. So the zero is a measured absence of Alabama's season geography, not a failed search.
AL.consequence: Alabama's licence is irrelevant to its blocker. The geography its regulations are written in — Deer Season Zones A-E and Turkey Season Zones 1-3 — is not published as GIS anywhere reachable, which is a different and more durable state than a licence refusal.

IA.supersedes: The earlier entry said there is no single zone identifier and Iowa needs a per-species geography model. Right, and it missed what the field names say.
IA.structure: Layer 'Hunting Regulations/Zones'. A POINT RESOLVES TO EXACTLY ONE FEATURE — Des Moines, Cedar Rapids and Sioux City each returned 1 — and the feature carries a zone value per species in its own column: NR_Deer, NR_S_Trky, R_F_Trky, CAGO, Waterfowl, Bobcat, Grouse. That is expressible today as one ZoneLayer per species over the same endpoint, each with its own nameField and speciesScope.
IA.theTrapInTheFieldNAMES: NR_Deer is NON-RESIDENT deer. R_F_Trky is RESIDENT fall turkey; NR_S_Trky is NON-RESIDENT spring turkey. IOWA ENCODES HUNTER CLASS INTO THE GEOGRAPHY, so serving NR_Deer as 'the deer zone' would hand a RESIDENT a non-resident's boundaries. Hunter class is a dimension of the opportunity, not of the map, and a layer cannot quietly carry one.
IA.andTheNonZoneVALUES: CAGO reads 'None', Grouse reads 'No', Bobcat reads 'No' or '1'. Those are not zone designations and `designationOf` must return null for them rather than minting a zone called No.
IA.whatIsCleanlyServable: Waterfowl — values North, Central, South — is hunter-class-neutral and is Iowa's real waterfowl zone system. It is the one column that can be served as a general zone layer without carrying a hunter class with it.

IL.supersedes: The earlier entry said a status string is not a zone id and IDNR publishes no umbrella zone system. Both true; the structure is better than that implied.
IL.structure: A point returns SIX features, one per species and season — Springfield and Chicago both did — each carrying Species, Season and Zone. Filtering on Species therefore yields exactly one zone per species, so this is a species-scoped layer by ROW where Louisiana's is by layer. Real values look like 'North Spring Turkey Hunting Zone', 'Central Duck & Goose Zone', 'South Upland Game Zone'.
IL.theTrapInTheZoneFIELD: THE SAME FIELD CARRIES ZONE IDENTITIES AND LEGAL CLOSURES. At Chicago, Zone reads 'No Spring Turkey Hunting Permitted' and 'No Bobcat Hunting or Trapping Permitted'; at Springfield, 'Closed to Fall Firearm Turkey Hunting'. A naive read mints a zone named after a prohibition and then resolves hunters into it. `designationOf` must reject every closure phrasing.
IL.andTheClosureIsNotNOTHING: It is the authority saying something real about that ground, and discarding it would be the other error. It is not the instrument either — a GIS attribute is not law, the same rule that governs Michigan's DMUs — so it belongs as evidence beside the UNKNOWN, never as a certified CLOSED.

LA.supersedes: The earlier entry said layer 3's only identifier was OBJECTID with no name field. That was wrong — it was read from a feature sample that happened not to surface Area_ID.
LA.evidence: Layer 3 is DeerManagementAreas: HTTP 200 anonymous, 166 ms, Query supported, 10 polygon features carrying Area_ID 1 to 10 — clean integer identifiers that map directly to canonical zone ids. The registry's recorded layer 0 is AlligatorHuntingZones.
LA.whyNotServedYet: ONE SERVICE, SEVEN SPECIES GEOGRAPHIES: layers 0-5 are Alligator, Dove, Goose, DeerManagementAreas, Waterfowl and Turkey. Serving the deer layer alone would put deer areas under a turkey question. The ZoneLayer model already handles this — `speciesScope` with `drawnByDefault`, as Newfoundland's moose, caribou and bear areas do — so this is a declaration per layer rather than new machinery, and it is the next Louisiana step.

robots.finding: No host disallows the service path. conservationgis.alabama.gov, geoservices3.dnr.illinois.gov and dwrmapserv.utah.gov return HTTP 404 for /robots.txt (no policy published); services1/services2.arcgis.com return 403 for /robots.txt, which is Esri's hosting platform rather than the authority and is not a statement about these datasets.

elidedServiceUrls.defect: Ten findings record a service URL with the organisation id replaced by '...', so the endpoint cannot be dereferenced from the registry. A recorded source that cannot be fetched is not provenance; §16 requires the service URL and §17 names a missing source URL as a failure mode. Found while recovering Connecticut's, which had the same defect.
elidedServiceUrls.howTheyWereRecovered: ArcGIS Online's public item search by the service name the elided URL still carried. The recovered item was then fetched and one feature read, because a title match is not a publisher match.
elidedServiceUrls.theTrapThisFound: Searching the WEST VIRGINIA service name returns, first, a service owned by wwagner@atcog.org — the Ark-Tex Council of Governments, a private regional body — whose own licenseInfo reads 'prepared for inclusion in the TPWD Wildlife database by Texas Parks and Wildlife' and whose accessInformation names Texas Parks and Wildlife Department. A title match would have attached TEXAS data to West Virginia with a plausible-looking licence. This is the 'a permissive licence can belong to another publisher entirely' hazard, and it is why each recovery below records the owner and whether the account is organisational.

CA.verified: HTTP 200. Layer 'Deer Hunt Zones - Title 14, Section 360 [ds342]'; a feature carries ZONE_LTR=B, Zone_Nam=B6 — the authority's own deer zones. copyrightText names the California Department of Fish and Wildlife.
CA.licenceIsNotSilent: Unlike the eight, CDFW states terms: 'These data should be used to estimate the general location of the hunting zone.' That is a legal-standing statement about accuracy and is recorded as such; it is not a reuse grant.
CA.confidence: HIGH — the only one of the ten on an organisational account with the authority named in its own copyright.

KS.verified: HTTP 200. A feature carries DMU='UNIT 8' — a clean deer management unit identifier, which is what a zone layer needs.
KS.licenceDescribesADIFFERENTTHING: Its licenseInfo is the U.S. Census TIGER/Line notice — the licence of the BASE COUNTY geometry it was built from, not KDWP's statement about its deer units. Reading it as the dataset's terms would be the 'licence of the tool, not the data' error in another costume.
KS.confidence: MEDIUM — the account name is the agency's but it is not an organisational account.

TN.verified: HTTP 200. The features carry COUNTY fields (CNTY_SP83_), consistent with the finding that Tennessee composes its Deer Management Units from counties rather than publishing unit polygons.
TN.confidence: MEDIUM — agency-shaped account name, not an organisational account.

WV.verified: HTTP 200, accessInformation 'WVDNR, WVGISTC'. BUT ITS FEATURES ARE PROPERTIES, NOT ZONES: Loc_Nm='Plum Orchard Lake', Category='Fee'. These are Wildlife Management AREAS, and West Virginia's recorded hunting geography is the COUNTY.
WV.confidence: RECOVERED BUT WRONG KIND — the same defect as Alabama's recorded layer: a real service that is not the geography the finding names.
